step.what: Restores the ordinary heating or cooling request after the filter inspection.
step.caution: Equipment can start. Do not restart for a fault, ice, water, an alarm, or an unusual smell or noise.
step.source: Second Wrench filter-check sequencing policy, October 12, 2026. Follow the exact equipment and thermostat manuals.
steps: With the specified filters in place and their access closed, restore only the thermostat settings you recorded. Keep equipment compartments closed.
Step away and allow at least five minutes for any normal thermostat delay. Do not repeatedly change modes or cycle power.
step.watch: If a warning appears, stop the check and use Stop / get help. If you cannot restore the prior settings, leave the request Off and call for assistance.
step.stop: Gas smell, a CO alarm, smoke, or possible refrigerant leakage means leave the affected area and get help; do not keep testing.
step.undo: If you’re not sure what you changed, put back what you wrote down. If you can’t, leave it and call a licensed HVAC professional. Don’t guess. For a hazard, follow the emergency instructions instead.
step.locked: Do not change wiring, equipment setup, safety controls, gas valves, fuses, or an outdoor disconnect. Do not open an equipment compartment.

steps: Record the thermostat settings, set the thermostat to Off, and wait for the blower to stop. This does not disconnect electricity.
Use only an external, tool-free owner filter slot or return grille identified by your manual and reachable from the floor. Do not open a furnace or air-handler compartment.
Replace a dirty disposable filter with the specified size and type in the manual’s direction and quantity. Do not wash a disposable filter or add extra stacked filters.
Close the filter access and leave the thermostat Off until the next hazard check.
step.watch: Do not run without the required filters. If you cannot finish, leave the request Off and call for service.
step.stop: Stop for ice, water near electrical parts, an unfamiliar access, or an unusual smell or sound. For gas, smoke, or a CO alarm, leave and call from outside.
step.undo: If you’re not sure what you changed, put back what you wrote down. If you can’t, leave it and call a licensed HVAC professional. Don’t guess. For a hazard, follow the emergency instructions instead.

step.what: Restoring electrical power may start equipment or energize its compressor heater.
step.caution: A misidentified breaker or a shutdown caused by a fault must not be overridden.
step.source: Second Wrench operator policy, October 11, 2026: one seasonal restoration and a 24-hour wait before cooling. The exact equipment manual takes priority; no generic tripped-breaker reset is offered.
steps: Record the thermostat settings and set the thermostat to Off.
Continue only with dry hands and a dry floor, no heat, buzzing, damage, burning smell, smoke, or water at the panel, and no tag, lock, or other person working on the equipment. Otherwise stop.
Open only the panel’s hinged door if needed. Leave the screwed-on protective cover in place. Touch only the clearly identified breaker handle and move it to On once.

Leave the thermostat Off for the wait specified by the exact manual. Second Wrench uses 24 hours before cooling after seasonal power restoration. If needed heating or cooling cannot wait, call for assistance instead of shortening the wait.
step.watch: If the breaker trips immediately or at the next equipment start, do not reset it. Leave it stopped and call a licensed HVAC professional or electrician.
step.stop: Stop for uncertainty about the breaker, why it was off, its prior trips, panel condition, or access. Do not use this step for a furnace breaker.
step.undo: If you’re not sure what you changed, put back what you wrote down. If you can’t, leave it and call a licensed HVAC professional. Don’t guess. For a hazard, follow the emergency instructions instead.

wshp.heat.cold_home_screen.title: Is the home getting too cold?
wshp.heat.cold_home_screen.body: Check the people and the home before the equipment. Read the room temperature without opening equipment. Is anyone at risk, is the temperature dropping, or could pipes freeze? The WHO housing guideline uses 18°C (64°F) as a minimum in cold seasons; vulnerable people may need a warmer home. This number does not rule out risk. If a faucet only trickles, a pipe may be frozen; call a plumber. Do not enter a crawlspace or thaw pipes with an open flame.

wshp_cold_exposure.title: Get the person warm first.
wshp_cold_exposure.explanation: Someone at risk from cold matters more than the equipment.
actions: If anyone is confused, very drowsy, or hard to wake, call 911 now.
If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first.
Add blankets and dry layers while getting help.
Bring pets somewhere warm too.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
Call a licensed geothermal or water-source heating professional once everyone is warm.
wshp_cold_exposure.avoid: Do not open equipment, reset a breaker, change water valves, or work on the well.

wshp_cold_home_urgent.title: The home needs heat. Call for service today.
wshp_cold_home_urgent.explanation: A cold or falling indoor temperature, uncertainty about its trend, or possible freezing pipes needs prompt attention.
actions: If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first.
If the house is still getting some heat, leave the thermostat on Heat.
If your thermostat has an Emergency Heat setting, switch to it to keep heat on with backup heat while you wait for a pro. It usually costs more to run.
An AUX indicator that comes on automatically is not the setting for Emergency Heat.
Bring pets somewhere warm too.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
Call a licensed geothermal or water-source professional today and describe the indoor temperature and trend. For a possible frozen pipe, call a plumber; never use an open flame.
wshp_cold_home_urgent.avoid: Do not open equipment, reset a breaker, change water valves, or work on the well.

wshp_well_water_out.title: Keep the heat pump from running without its water supply.
wshp_well_water_out.explanation: You reported an open-loop system and weak or missing house well water. Neither the well condition nor water flow through the unit has been confirmed.
actions: Use Off at the thermostat, or Emergency Heat if the system has that backup-only setting, while arranging service. Do not use normal Heat or Cool without the required water supply.
An automatic AUX light is not the setting for Emergency Heat. Do not change a valve, open the well controls, or reset a breaker.
If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
Tell the geothermal service company and well professional that the water supply is weak or unavailable.
Source: WaterFurnace Residential Owner’s Manual OM1500MW, page 13, Water Supply; checked October 12, 2026.

steps: 1. Write down how the thermostat is set, then turn the system Off at the thermostat. This doesn’t cut power to the unit, so stay outside the grilles. 2. Move planters, toys, covers, and stored items away from the unit. 3. Trim plants back by hand or with hand pruners, keeping the pruners and clippings away from the unit. 4. Pick up loose leaves and clippings from the ground around the unit. Don’t touch the coil or fins at all, by hand or with any tool. Don’t reach through the grille, use a pressure washer, or spray water near the electrical side. Leave anything on the fins, stuck in them, or behind the grille for a professional. 5. Put the thermostat back the way you wrote it down.
step.watch: After you set the thermostat back, watch from a few steps back for about 10 minutes.
step.stop: Stop and put the thermostat back the way you wrote it down if anything near the electrical box is wet or icy, if you’d have to reach inside the grille, or if the fan starts while you’re close. If that doesn’t fix it, call a licensed HVAC professional.
step.undo: If you’re not sure what you changed, put back the thermostat settings you wrote down. If you can’t, leave it and call a licensed HVAC professional.
step.locked: Don’t change these. They protect your equipment and your safety, and they’re for professionals only: any side, top, or front panel or cover; the electrical or control box; the disconnect box and its handle or fuses; buttons, switches, or displays on the board inside the unit; the fan blade and fan motor; refrigerant valves, caps, and pipes; the pipe cover and insulation; the stand, wall bracket, and their bolts; any heater, sensor, or wire on the unit; service menus and anything that clears or deletes stored codes or error history. If a step would take you to one of these, stop. If a screen asks you to enter a password or access code, stop. That’s for installers. Writing down an error code that’s already showing is fine.

step.what: What this does: Moves loose snow away from the unit so it can breathe and defrost water can drain. Caution: Snow and ice around the unit are slippery, and the fins bend easily.
step.caution: Snow and ice around the unit are slippery, and the fins bend easily.
step.source: From Daikin 3P515859-5S (p. 6), Bosch BOVA20 IOM (§2.3), and NEEP’s cold-climate install guide, checked October 11, 2026.
steps: 1. Only go out if you can stand on cleared, level ground in daylight. Don’t use a ladder or climb a snowbank. 2. Write down how the thermostat is set, then turn the system Off at the thermostat. 3. Clear loose snow from the ground around the unit and in front of the fan, by hand or with a soft broom, so air can move and defrost water can drain. Don’t clear snow off the coil or fins, and don’t touch them at all, by hand or with any tool. They bend easily. 4. Don’t use a shovel or snowblower near the unit, and don’t pile snow against it. 5. Leave ice alone: don’t chip, pry, or hit it, and don’t use hot water, a heat gun, or a torch. 6. Put the thermostat back the way you wrote it down.
step.watch: After you set the thermostat back, watch from inside for up to 15 minutes. A cloud of steam and a stopped outdoor fan can be part of a normal defrost.
step.stop: Stop if snow or ice is packed against the electrical box or disconnect, if there’s ice inside the grille, or if the footing is icy, and call a licensed HVAC professional. If ice is building up on the coil or the unit is encased in ice, leave the system Off at the thermostat, don’t chip the ice, and call a licensed HVAC professional.
step.undo: If you’re not sure what you changed, put back the thermostat settings you wrote down. If you can’t, leave it and call a licensed HVAC professional.
step.locked: Don’t change these. ms.controls.mode_setpoint.title: Check the settings first
ms.controls.mode_setpoint.body:
Use the remote, wall control, or app you already use. Don’t open the indoor unit.

1. Mode is Cool (a snowflake on many remotes). If it says Auto, Dry, Fan, or Heat, switch it to Cool for this check.
2. The temperature is set at least 3°F below the room. In Cool, many units won’t start cooling if the setting is at or above room temperature.
3. Fan is Auto or High, not Quiet, Silent, or Night.
4. Timers, Sleep, and app schedules are off for now.
5. If your remote has Follow Me or I Feel, keep the remote in the same room.

After any change, wait 5 to 10 minutes. Many mini-splits run the fan slowly for the first few minutes.

Remote screen blank? You can put in fresh batteries if the battery cover slides off by hand and nothing is cracked or leaking.

options.hint: Simple fix. We’ll show what to watch for.

ms.heat.defrost_sanity.title: Is this a normal defrost, or ice that stays?
ms.heat.defrost_sanity.body:
In Heat, a mini-split sometimes pauses to clear frost from the outdoor unit. From inside, heating stops for a while, the indoor fan stops or slows, and a light may blink. You may hear a whoosh. The remote may not change the mode until that pause ends. Leave it in Heat. Don’t switch modes during the pause.

 A normal defrost usually lasts about 5 to 15 minutes, and some models finish sooner. Ice that is still there after about an hour of running is not normal. Call a licensed HVAC professional.

 While it defrosts, the outdoor fan often stops and steam can rise from the unit. Don’t try to speed it up.
 In cold weather, a cloud of steam from the outdoor unit during defrost can be normal. If you’re not sure it’s steam, or you smell burning, treat it as smoke.
 If so, choose that option. A cloud from the indoor unit in Heat isn’t a defrost. Choose that option too.
 Not normal: a solid block of ice that keeps growing, a grille iced shut, or ice that never clears.

 Don’t chip or pick at ice, use hot water, a hose, a heat gun, a hair dryer, or salt, or cover the unit.

 Look from a window or from dry, cleared ground. Don’t reach into the grille. Don’t go out in ice, deep snow, or the dark to get a closer look.

If ice is thick, growing, or closes the grille, stop now. Do not keep the system running to time an hour.

Outside, a cloud of steam can rise from the outdoor unit while it defrosts, and that can be normal. Ice that stays on the outdoor unit and keeps building isn’t a normal defrost. Look from a step back, and don’t touch the unit.

ms.head.filter_clean.title: Clean the filters the way your manual shows
ms.head.filter_clean.body:
1. Keep the unit Off with the remote. You checked that it stopped and no ice or water was visible.
2. Lift the front cover by hand, the way the manual shows.
3. Slide the filters out. If the manual says a part shouldn’t get wet, keep it dry.
4. Vacuum the dust off, or rinse with lukewarm water, never hotter than 104°F (40°C). Use mild soap only if the manual allows it. Don’t wring them.
5. Let washed filters dry fully in the shade.
6. Slide them back in and close the cover until it’s fully shut.

Remote Off doesn’t cut the power. Touch only the filters and the cover. Don’t reach past them, and don’t spray anything on the parts inside.

Run it only with the filters in place.

step.what: Sets every indoor unit on this outdoor unit to the same mode as the one with the problem, so the outdoor unit isn’t asked to heat and cool at once.
step.caution: A room you set to Off won’t be heated or cooled until you turn it back on. In cold weather, set every unit to Heat instead of turning a room Off. If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first.
step.source: Senville mode-conflict guidance and Pioneer Quantum Ultra PA guidance; checked October 12, 2026. The ten-minute observation period is Second Wrench policy.
step.watch: The unit with the problem, for 10 minutes.
step.stop: If a code returns, the unit stops again, water or ice appears, or another room loses needed heat, stop this check and call a professional. Restore only ordinary comfort settings when no hazard is present. Never restart a faulted unit as an undo step.
step.undo: If you’re not sure what you changed, put back what you wrote down. If you can’t, leave it and call a licensed HVAC professional. Don’t guess.
steps: Check the mode on every indoor unit that shares this outdoor unit, including rooms no one is using.
Set each one to the same mode as the unit with the problem: all Heat, or all Cool. If a room shouldn’t run, you can turn that unit Off instead. Don’t set any unit to the opposite mode.
Don’t use Auto on any of them for now. Auto can pick the opposite mode on its own.
Wait 10 minutes, then check the unit with the problem.
step.locked: Don’t change these. They protect your equipment and your safety, and they’re for professionals only: installer or service menus, unit addresses or priority, switches on the unit, electrical or refrigerant parts, stored error codes or history, and any setting behind a panel. If a step would take you to one of these, stop. If a screen asks you to enter a password or access code, stop. That’s for installers.

ms.sound.observe.title: Is that sound normal?
ms.sound.observe.body:
Often normal on a mini-split:
• A gurgle, trickle, or short hiss, like water moving, mostly in the first few minutes after it starts or stops. That’s fluid moving through the pipes inside.
• A light crack, creak, snap, or tick when it starts, stops, or changes temperature. That’s plastic parts growing and shrinking.
• A soft click or tap when the louver moves.
• A dripping sound for a little while after it turns off.
• In Heat: a whoosh or sizzle, with the indoor fan stopping for a few minutes. That’s often a defrost.

Not normal: grinding, scraping, rattling, squealing, a loud bang, a high whine, a hiss that doesn’t stop, or a sound that keeps getting louder.

A steady hiss from the indoor unit that doesn’t stop gets its own answer below. 

Buzzing, popping, or crackling from the cord, an outlet, or the unit’s wires, or any sound with a burning smell or smoke, is a hazard. Choose that answer.

steps: Stand in the same room, within the range in your exact remote manual, and point the remote at the indoor unit. Many units beep when they get a signal. Curtains, direct sun, and bright fluorescent or neon light can block it.
Look for a lock symbol on the remote screen. If your manual shows how to unlock it, do that.

Batteries: only if the battery cover slides off by hand and nothing is cracked or leaking. Use the type your manual lists, all new and all the same kind, and match + and −. If your remote charges by cable, charge it the way the manual shows.

After new batteries, some remotes go back to their factory signal code and stop talking to the unit. Dry: if you want cooling, use Cool instead. Dry runs the fan slowly and can pause it. It isn’t a heating mode.

ms.heat.defrost_indoor.section: Heat stopped for a few minutes? Check for a defrost from inside
ms.heat.defrost_indoor.title: Heat stopped for a few minutes? Check for a defrost from inside
ms.heat.defrost_indoor.body:
In Heat, a mini-split pauses now and then to melt frost off the outdoor unit. From inside, a normal pause can look like this:
• The indoor fan stops or slows, and no warm air comes out for a few minutes. Fujitsu lists up to 15 minutes for one model (Operating Manual 9/12/15RLS3, p. 7). Check your unit’s manual.
• A light on the indoor unit blinks, or the display shows a defrost symbol. Your manual shows which.
• The louver stops moving or drops to its lowest spot.
• The remote may not change anything until the pause ends.

Then heat comes back on its own. Leave it in Heat. Don’t switch modes, press buttons on the unit, or turn it off and on to hurry it.

Lennox DB68-12580A-00, page 28, describes a 3–5 minute warm-up fan delay and defrost lasting 5–12 minutes for that model; checked October 12, 2026. Other models differ.

ms.head.shutdown_thaw_check.section: Before you open the cover: is it fully off, with no ice?
ms.head.shutdown_thaw_check.title: Before you open the cover: is it fully off, with no ice?
ms.head.shutdown_thaw_check.body:
1. Write down or photograph the current mode, temperature, fan, and timer settings. Then turn the unit Off with the remote, wall control, or app.
2. Wait until it has fully stopped: the fan is still and the louver has closed. This can take a minute or two.
3. From the floor, look at the front of the unit and the air outlet. Check for ice or frost, and for water dripping.

Turning the unit off with the remote stops it running. It doesn’t cut the power. Don’t open the cover until it has fully stopped.

ms.head.condensate_outside.title: Water dripping outside the house?
ms.head.condensate_outside.body:
When a mini-split cools or dries the air, it pulls water out of it. A small hose or pipe usually carries that water outside. A steady drip from that hose on a warm, humid day is normal. No drip on a dry day, or for the first few minutes, can be normal too.

Water coming from the outdoor unit itself while it heats is a different thing. That’s often melted frost.

ms.zone.mode_conflict.section: Two indoor units asking for opposite things
ms.zone.mode_conflict.title: Two indoor units asking for opposite things
ms.zone.mode_conflict.caution: Use only each unit’s own remote or the app. Don’t change addresses, priority, or settings on the outdoor unit.

step.what: Sets every indoor unit on the same outdoor unit to the same mode, or to Off, so the outdoor unit isn’t asked to cool and heat at once.
step.caution: A room you set to Off won’t be heated or cooled until you turn it back on. In cold weather, set every unit to Heat instead of turning a room Off. If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first.
step.source: Senville mode-conflict guidance and Pioneer Quantum Ultra PA guidance; checked October 12, 2026. The ten-minute observation period is Second Wrench policy.
step.watch: If the conflict code or blinking clears and the unit starts, for 10 minutes.
step.stop: If a code returns, the unit stops again, water or ice appears, or another room loses needed heat, stop this check and call a professional. Restore only ordinary comfort settings when no hazard is present. Never restart a faulted unit as an undo step.
step.undo: If you’re not sure what you changed, put back what you wrote down. If you can’t, leave it and call a licensed HVAC professional. Don’t guess.
steps: Check the mode on every indoor unit that shares this outdoor unit, including rooms no one is using.
Set them all to Cool, or all to Heat. If a room shouldn’t run, turn that unit Off. Don’t set it to the opposite mode.
Don’t use Auto on any of them for now. Auto can pick the opposite mode on its own.
Wait 10 minutes.
step.locked: Don’t change these. They protect your equipment and your safety, and they’re for professionals only: installer or service menus, unit addresses or priority, switches on the unit, electrical or refrigerant parts, stored error codes or history, and any setting behind a panel. If a step would take you to one of these, stop. If a screen asks you to enter a password or access code, stop. That’s for installers.

ms.head.filter_power_off.title: Before you clean the filters
ms.head.filter_power_off.body: Turn the system Off at the thermostat. Then switch off its breaker (or the outdoor disconnect or service switch near the unit). When you're done and everything is dry, switch it back on. If a breaker trips again or keeps tripping, leave it off and call a licensed HVAC professional. Never open the breaker panel cover or the disconnect box.

ms.head.pause_guard.title: Can you leave this unit Off through cleaning and drying?
ms.head.pause_guard.body: Washed filters must dry fully before the unit runs again. This can take much longer than a brief stop. Do not begin if anyone needs uninterrupted heating or cooling, the home is getting too cold or hot, pipes may freeze, or you are unsure how long you can leave it Off. Arrange a professional visit instead.

ms_use_central_check.title: This path is for ductless mini-splits.
ms_use_central_check.explanation: A system with vents and ducts has its own check.
actions: Go back home, press Start, and choose Cooling-only AC or Heat pump.
ms_use_central_check.avoid: Don’t remove a cover to re-check the equipment.

ms_equipment_oos.title: This equipment isn’t covered here.
ms_equipment_oos.explanation: Window, portable, and through-the-wall units, and other types, aren’t diagnosed in this beta.
actions: Use the maker’s owner guidance, or a technician who works on that type of unit.
If you already know the model number, write it down. Don’t remove a cover or climb to find it.
ms_equipment_oos.avoid: Don’t apply this mini-split guide to other equipment.

ms_system_unconfirmed.title: This check needs a confirmed ductless mini-split.
ms_system_unconfirmed.explanation: Guessing the equipment type can send you down the wrong steps.
actions: Check the owner’s manual, or ask someone who knows the equipment.
Start again when you can confirm it. If you can’t, call an HVAC company rather than guessing.
ms_system_unconfirmed.avoid: Don’t remove covers or climb to read labels.

ms_settings_fixed_basic.title: A setting was the problem.
ms_settings_fixed_basic.explanation: Cool mode, a setting below the room, and a normal fan speed let the mini-split cool the way it should.
actions: Leave it in Cool, not Auto, while you need cooling.
If you use Quiet, Sleep, or a schedule, check that it isn’t turning cooling off when you need it.
If it stops cooling again with the right settings, start a new check and choose Not cooling.
ms_settings_fixed_basic.avoid: Don’t change installer settings or open the unit.

ms_no_response_wave1.title: The unit isn’t responding to its controls.
ms_no_response_wave1.explanation: When the remote or app can’t control it, or the indoor unit shows no lights, the cause can be power, wiring, or the controls inside. Those are pro checks.
actions: Call a licensed HVAC pro. Tell them whether the indoor unit shows any lights, and whether fresh remote batteries helped.
If you smell burning or see smoke or sparks, get people away and call 911 from safety.
ms_no_response_wave1.avoid: Don’t open the indoor or outdoor unit, rewire anything, or reset breakers to test it.

ms_controls_unsure.title: The next steps depend on the remote or app settings.
ms_controls_unsure.explanation: If the remote screen is hard to read, the app or the owner’s manual can show the current mode and setting.
actions: Look at the app, or the remote in good light, and note the mode, temperature, and fan setting.
Start again when you can see them. If you can’t read them at all, call an HVAC pro.
ms_controls_unsure.avoid: Don’t open the unit to look for settings.

ms_filter_inaccessible.title: Skip a filter step you can’t do.
ms_filter_inaccessible.explanation: Let a professional handle filters that are out of reach from the floor, need tools or force, or require unplugging. If you are not sure remote Off is enough, stop here too.
actions: If a cover is partly open, leave it and keep the unit Off with the remote.
From the floor, move curtains or furniture away from the indoor unit.
Call a licensed HVAC pro and ask them to clean the filters and check airflow. Tell them how the system is acting.
ms_filter_inaccessible.avoid: Don’t climb a ladder, chair, or stool, pry the cover, or run the unit without filters.

ms_filter_path_unconfirmed.title: The filter step waits on your owner’s manual.
ms_filter_path_unconfirmed.explanation: Covers and clips differ by model. Guessing can break them.
actions: If you already know the model number, look up the owner’s manual from the maker. Don’t climb or remove a cover to find it.
Start a new check when you have the filter steps, or ask an HVAC pro to clean the filters.
ms_filter_path_unconfirmed.avoid: Don’t pry or force the front cover.

ms_filter_drying_basic.urgency: Finish when the filters are dry
ms_filter_drying_basic.title: Washed filters need to dry fully first.
ms_filter_drying_basic.explanation: Let them dry in the shade, not in the sun or with a heater or hair dryer.
actions: Before restarting, fully dry and refit the specified filters and close the cover. For ice, water, a code, or another hazard, leave it Off and use Stop / get help.
Leave the unit Off until the filters are back in. Run it only with the filters in place.
When they’re dry, slide them back in and close the cover all the way.
Run it in the mode you need for about 15 minutes. If the air is still weak, or the room still isn’t comfortable, start a new check.
ms_filter_drying_basic.avoid: Don’t use heat to dry them, and don’t run the unit without filters.

ms_filter_replace_basic.title: A filter is torn, damaged, or missing.
ms_filter_replace_basic.explanation: Replacement filters are made for each model. The maker or your installer can tell you which one fits.
actions: Before restarting, fully dry and refit the specified filters and close the cover. For ice, water, a code, or another hazard, leave it Off and use Stop / get help.
Order the replacement filter for your model from the maker or a dealer.
Most manuals say not to run the unit without its filters. Follow yours until the new one arrives.
Put the new filter in the way the manual shows. If it doesn’t fit, don’t force it. Call your installer.
ms_filter_replace_basic.avoid: Don’t trim a different filter to fit, and don’t force the cover.

ms_head_cleaning_pro.title: Buildup inside the indoor unit is a pro cleaning job.
ms_head_cleaning_pro.explanation: Mold, slime, or heavy dirt inside the unit needs a pro cleaning. Spray cleaners and bleach can damage the unit.
actions: Close the cover. Leave the unit Off if the air smells musty or bad.
Call a licensed HVAC pro and ask for an indoor-unit cleaning. Tell them what you saw.
Keep cleaning the washable filters on the schedule in your manual.
ms_head_cleaning_pro.avoid: Don’t spray cleaners, bleach, or water into the unit, or take it apart.

ms_louver_stuck.title: The louver won’t move with the remote.
ms_louver_stuck.explanation: Forcing a louver by hand can break it. A pro can check the louver and what drives it.
actions: Leave the louver where it is.
If air still comes out, you can keep using the unit. If the louver is closed and blocking the air, turn it Off with the remote.
Call a licensed HVAC pro and tell them what the louver does.
ms_louver_stuck.avoid: Don’t push, pry, or bend the louver, or open the unit.

ms_airflow_improved_basic.title: The basic checks brought the air back.
ms_airflow_improved_basic.explanation: Clean filters and a clear path in front of the unit are common fixes for weak air.
actions: Clean the filters as often as your manual says. Many say every two weeks when it runs a lot.
Keep curtains and furniture clear of the indoor unit.
If the air gets weak again soon after cleaning, or you see ice or water, start a new check.
ms_airflow_improved_basic.avoid: Don’t spray cleaners into the unit or open it past the filters.

ms_weak_air_after_basics.title: Air is still weak after the basic checks.
ms_weak_air_after_basics.explanation: Settings, filters, and a clear path are done. What’s left is inside the unit, and that needs a pro. This isn’t a confirmed diagnosis.
actions: If you see ice or water, or it isn’t cooling or heating, turn it Off with the remote.
Call a licensed HVAC pro. Tell them what you checked: settings, filters, and anything blocking the unit.
Your service note below lists what you told this check.
ms_weak_air_after_basics.avoid: Don’t open the unit, spray cleaners inside, or add refrigerant.

ms_no_cool_after_basics.title: Air is moving, but it isn’t cooling.
ms_no_cool_after_basics.explanation: Settings, filters, and a clear path are done. When strong air still isn’t cold, the cause needs a pro to test. This isn’t a confirmed diagnosis.
actions: Turn it Off with the remote so it doesn’t run without cooling.
Call a licensed HVAC pro. Tell them the settings, filter, and airflow checks you did.
If someone in the home becomes confused, faint, or seriously ill from the heat, call 911.
ms_no_cool_after_basics.avoid: Don’t add refrigerant, open the outdoor unit, or reset breakers to test it.

ms_airflow_unsure.title: The airflow check needs a clearer answer.
ms_airflow_unsure.explanation: It’s fine not to know. Don’t open the unit to find out.
actions: Use the mode you need, only while everyone has enough heating or cooling, and observe for up to 15 minutes.
Start a new check if it’s still unclear, or call an HVAC pro and describe what you noticed.
ms_airflow_unsure.avoid: Don’t open the unit or put anything into the air outlet.

ms_condensate_leak_wave1.title: Water from the indoor unit needs a pro.
ms_condensate_leak_wave1.explanation: The water usually comes from the drain that carries water away from the unit. Clearing or fixing the drain, pump, or pan is a pro job.
actions: Turn the unit Off with the remote to stop new water. Remote Off doesn’t cut the power, so stay away from the unit’s wiring.
Put towels or a bucket under it. Keep water away from outlets and cords.
Call a licensed HVAC pro. Tell them where the water is and how much.
If water reaches an outlet, cord, or light, stay clear and call a pro or electrician.
If you see sparks or smoke, or smell burning, get out and call 911 from outside.
ms_condensate_leak_wave1.avoid: Don’t open the unit, pour bleach, vinegar, or other chemicals into the drain, push anything through it, or drill holes.

ms_error_code_wave1.title: Give the code to a pro.
ms_error_code_wave1.explanation: Error codes point a pro to what to check. They aren’t a homeowner repair list, and the same code can mean different things on different brands.
actions: If it isn’t cooling, or the code keeps coming back, turn it Off with the remote.
Call a licensed HVAC pro, or the installer or maker. Give them the code or light pattern, when it showed, and what the unit was doing.
If you couldn’t read it from the floor, say so. Don’t climb to read it.
ms_error_code_wave1.avoid: Don’t follow repair steps from a code list.

ms_ice_cooling_wave1.urgency: Turn it off · call a pro
ms_ice_cooling_wave1.title: Turn it off and let the ice melt.
ms_ice_cooling_wave1.explanation: Running a mini-split with ice on it can damage it, and the melt can drip. A dirty filter can cause ice, and so can problems only a pro can check.
actions: Turn the unit Off with the remote or app.
Put towels or a bucket under the indoor unit. Keep water away from outlets and cords.
Let the ice melt on its own. It can take a few hours.
Call a licensed HVAC pro. Tell them where you saw ice and when the filters were last cleaned.
If water reaches an outlet, cord, or light, stay clear and call a pro or electrician.
If you see sparks or smoke, or smell burning, get out and call 911 from outside.
ms_ice_cooling_wave1.avoid: Don’t chip or pick at the ice, or use a hair dryer, heat gun, hot water, a hose, or salt, or cover the unit. Don’t restart cooling while any ice remains.

ms_ice_keep_running.title: Stop. Turn it off and let the ice melt.
ms_ice_keep_running.explanation: Running a mini-split with ice on it, or restarting it too soon, can damage it. Melting ice can drip from the indoor unit.
actions: Turn the unit Off with the remote or app.
Put towels or a bucket under the indoor unit. Keep water away from outlets and cords.
Don’t open the front cover or any panel to check the ice.
Leave it off and call a licensed HVAC pro.
If water reaches an outlet or cord, stay clear and call a pro or electrician.
ms_ice_keep_running.avoid: Don’t chip or pick at the ice, use a hair dryer, heat gun, hot water, a hose, or salt, cover the unit, or keep restarting it.

ms_ice_unclear_or_heat.title: This check can’t sort out this ice yet.
ms_ice_unclear_or_heat.explanation: Light frost while heating can be normal briefly. A normal defrost usually lasts about 5 to 15 minutes, and some models finish sooner. Ice that is still there after about an hour of running is not normal. Call a licensed HVAC professional.
actions: For thick or growing ice, turn the unit Off with the remote and call a professional now. Do not keep it running to time an hour.
If you cannot tell whether it is ice, describe the observation from a window or dry ground to a professional.

If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first. Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
ms_ice_unclear_or_heat.avoid: Don’t chip or pick at ice, use hot water, a hose, a heat gun, a hair dryer, or salt, or cover the unit. Don’t open the outdoor unit.

ms_hazard_now.title: A new hazard ends this check.
ms_hazard_now.explanation: Gas, smoke, sparks, a burning smell, or water at electrical equipment is not a mini-split DIY path.
actions: If you smell gas or a carbon monoxide alarm is sounding, leave the building and call for help from outside. Do not operate switches inside.
If there is smoke, fire, or sparks, get people away and call 911 from safety.

If a refrigerant leak alarm is going off, move people out of the affected area to fresh air without operating switches or creating ignition sources. Don’t reset the alarm, cycle power, or turn off a blower that’s running. Call a licensed HVAC professional from outside the affected area, and for breathing trouble or immediate danger, call 911.
If water is at electrical equipment, stay clear and don’t touch anything. Leave the area and call a licensed HVAC pro or an electrician.
Do not return to troubleshooting until the hazard has been handled.
ms_hazard_now.avoid: Do not keep diagnosing, open covers, or touch wet equipment.

ms_unsure_water_electrical.title: Don’t touch the indoor unit to find out.
ms_unsure_water_electrical.explanation: If you can’t tell whether water or melting ice is near an outlet, a cord, or the unit’s wiring, stop.
actions: Stay clear of the indoor unit and any wet floor. Don’t touch the unit, a switch, a cord, or the breaker panel.
Leave the area and call a licensed HVAC pro or an electrician. Tell them what you already saw.
If you see sparks or smoke, or smell burning, get out and call 911 from outside.
ms_unsure_water_electrical.avoid: Don’t mop around the unit, and don’t touch the breaker panel.

ms_water_electrical.title: Don’t touch the indoor unit or stand in the water.
ms_water_electrical.explanation: Water is on or near the mini-split’s electrical parts.
actions: Don’t touch the indoor unit, any switch, a cord, or the breaker panel, and don’t stand in the water.
Leave the area, keep others and pets away, and call a licensed HVAC pro or an electrician.
If you see sparks, smoke, or smell burning, get out and call 911 from outside.
ms_water_electrical.avoid: Don’t touch the indoor unit, any switch, or the breaker panel.

ms_heat_settings_fixed_basic.title: Leave it in Heat.
ms_heat_settings_fixed_basic.explanation: Heat mode, a setting above the room, and a normal fan let the mini-split heat the way it should. A short warm-up is normal. So is an occasional defrost pause.
actions: Leave it in Heat, not Auto, while you need heat.
Expect a short warm-up. The indoor fan may wait a few minutes so it doesn’t blow cold air.
An occasional pause with steam and a whoosh can be a normal defrost. If ice stays or keeps building, turn it Off with the remote and call a licensed HVAC pro.
ms_heat_settings_fixed_basic.avoid: Don’t change installer settings, open the unit, or switch modes during a defrost pause.

ms_heat_auto_fixed_basic.title: Heat, not Auto, was the fix.
ms_heat_auto_fixed_basic.explanation: Auto had the unit off Heat. Setting Heat and waiting brought the heat back.
actions: Leave it in Heat, not Auto, during heating season.
If it stops heating again with Heat set, start a new check and choose Not heating.

If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first. Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
ms_heat_auto_fixed_basic.avoid: Don’t leave it on Auto when you need steady heat.

ms_defrost_normal_basic.title: That pause was a normal defrost.
ms_defrost_normal_basic.explanation: You reported a pause followed by heat returning. Steam, a pause, and a whoosh can match defrost, but do not confirm system performance. A normal defrost usually lasts about 5 to 15 minutes, and some models finish sooner. Ice that is still there after about an hour of running is not normal. Call a licensed HVAC professional.
actions: Leave it in Heat. Don’t switch modes during a defrost pause.
If ice stays, keeps building, or heat doesn’t return after about an hour, turn it Off with the remote and call a licensed HVAC pro.

If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first. Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
ms_defrost_normal_basic.avoid: Don’t chip or pick at ice, use hot water, a hose, a heat gun, a hair dryer, or salt, or cover the unit.

ms_outdoor_running_call_pro.title: The outdoor unit is running, and the room still isn’t comfortable.
ms_outdoor_running_call_pro.explanation: A pro needs to test the system. This isn’t a diagnosis.
actions: You can leave it in Heat if some heat is coming. If no useful heat is coming, turn it Off with the remote.
Call a licensed HVAC pro. Tell them the outdoor unit was running and the room was still not comfortable.

If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first. Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.

ms_outdoor_not_running_wave1.title: The outdoor unit is quiet while a unit is calling.
ms_outdoor_not_running_wave1.explanation: When an indoor unit is asking for heat or cool and the outdoor unit stays quiet, the cause needs a pro. This isn’t a diagnosis.
actions: Leave the indoor unit as it is, or turn it Off with the remote.
Call a licensed HVAC pro. Tell them the indoor unit was calling and the outdoor unit was quiet.

If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first. Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
ms_outdoor_not_running_wave1.avoid: Don’t reset a breaker, open a disconnect, or cover the outdoor unit.

ms_outdoor_freeze_heat_wave1.title: Stop. Turn it off. Thick ice won’t clear by running it.
ms_outdoor_freeze_heat_wave1.explanation: Ice that stays or keeps building is not a normal defrost. Running it iced can damage it. Most mini-splits have no separate emergency heat.
actions: Turn the unit Off with the remote or app.

If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first. Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
Call a licensed HVAC pro once everyone is warm.
ms_outdoor_freeze_heat_wave1.avoid: Don’t chip or pick at ice, use hot water, a hose, a heat gun, a hair dryer, or salt, or cover the unit. Don’t keep the iced unit running.

ms_ice_heat_keep_running.title: Stop. Turn it off. Don’t run it iced to force heat.
ms_ice_heat_keep_running.explanation: Running an iced outdoor unit to force heat can damage it. Most mini-splits have no separate emergency heat.
actions: Turn the unit Off with the remote or app.

If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first. Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
Call a licensed HVAC pro once everyone is warm.
ms_ice_heat_keep_running.avoid: Don’t chip or pick at ice, use hot water, a hose, a heat gun, a hair dryer, or salt, or cover the unit. Don’t keep the iced unit running.

ms_cold_exposure.urgency: Get warm now · call 911 if needed
ms_cold_exposure.title: Get the person warm first.
ms_cold_exposure.explanation: Someone at risk from the cold matters more than the mini-split.
actions: If anyone is confused, very drowsy, or hard to wake, call 911 now.
Otherwise, get them somewhere warm: a neighbor, family, or a warming center.
Add blankets and dry layers in the meantime.

If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first. Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
Call a licensed HVAC pro for the mini-split once everyone is warm.
ms_cold_exposure.avoid: Don’t wait on a mini-split repair to get someone warm.

ms_heat_not_supported.title: This remote may have no heat.
ms_heat_not_supported.explanation: If the remote or app has no Heat setting, the unit may be cooling-only. This check won’t guess that it can heat.
actions: Check the owner’s manual for the model you already know. Don’t open a cover or climb to find a model number.
If the manual has no Heat mode, call a licensed HVAC pro rather than guessing.

If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first. Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
ms_heat_not_supported.avoid: Don’t force a mode the remote doesn’t offer, and don’t open the unit.

ms_heat_wait_unsure.title: Wait the full 10 to 15 minutes, then check again.
ms_heat_wait_unsure.explanation: Heat can take 10 to 15 minutes, and the indoor fan may stay off at first. Stopping early can look like no heat.
actions: Leave it in Heat, at least 3°F above the room, and wait the full 10 to 15 minutes.
Start a new check after that if it still isn’t heating.

If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first. Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
ms_heat_wait_unsure.avoid: Don’t switch modes during the wait, and don’t open the unit.

ms_outdoor_unsure.urgency: Stop where you can see from where I stand
ms_outdoor_unsure.title: Don’t go closer to see the outdoor unit.
ms_outdoor_unsure.explanation: If you can’t see it from a window or from dry, cleared ground, stop there. Icy ground, deep snow, and darkness are reasons not to go out.
actions: Stay inside. Describe what you already know to a licensed HVAC pro.

If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first. Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
ms_outdoor_unsure.avoid: Don’t climb, reach into the grille, or go out in unsafe conditions to look.

ms_outdoor_water_electrical.title: Don’t touch the outdoor unit or stand in the water.
ms_outdoor_water_electrical.explanation: Water, melt, or ice is on or near the outdoor unit’s power box, cord, or outlet.
actions: Don’t touch the outdoor unit, any switch, a cord, or the breaker panel, and don’t stand in the water.
Leave the area, keep others and pets away, and call a licensed HVAC pro or an electrician.
If you see sparks, smoke, or smell burning, get out and call 911 from outside.
ms_outdoor_water_electrical.avoid: Don’t touch the outdoor unit, any switch, or the breaker panel.

ms_advanced_off.title: Capacitor, contactor, inverter, and board work are not offered on a mini-split in this beta.
ms_advanced_off.explanation: These jobs need a licensed HVAC professional.
actions: Leave covers on.
Call a licensed HVAC professional. Tell them what the unit was doing and that you did not remove covers.
ms_advanced_off.avoid: Do not start a capacitor, contactor, inverter, or board repair from this mini-split check.

ms_after_outage_normal_basic.title: You reported that it started after the wait.
ms_after_outage_normal_basic.explanation: Many mini-splits wait a few minutes after power comes back, then start again with the settings they had.
actions: If you used a timer or schedule, check it’s still set. Outages can clear timers.
If it stops again, or a code shows, start a new check and choose the code option.
ms_after_outage_normal_basic.avoid: Don’t reset breakers or switches to hurry it.

ms_sound_normal_basic.title: That sounds like a normal mini-split noise.
ms_sound_normal_basic.explanation: Gurgles, light cracks, louver clicks, and defrost whooshes are common and usually fade within a few minutes.
actions: Note when you hear it, and in which mode.
If it gets louder, changes to grinding or rattling, or comes with a smell, start a new check.
ms_sound_normal_basic.avoid: Don’t open the unit to find the sound.

ms_sound_pro.title: That sound needs a pro to look at it.
ms_sound_pro.explanation: Grinding, scraping, rattling, squealing, a bang, or a sound that keeps getting louder can mean a part is loose or wearing out inside. A hiss that doesn’t stop can mean a leak.
actions: For a steady outdoor hiss, turn the unit Off with the remote and call a professional. For an indoor chemical smell, steady indoor hiss, or a leak alarm, leave the affected area and use Stop / get help.
Turn the unit off with the remote if the sound is loud or getting worse.
Tell the pro what the sound is like, when it happens, and the mode.
If you see sparks or smoke, or smell burning, get out and call 911 from outside.
ms_sound_pro.avoid: Don’t open the unit or keep running it to see if the sound goes away.

ms_sound_unsure.urgency: Listen again, or call a pro
ms_sound_unsure.title: Hard to tell from here.
ms_sound_unsure.explanation: Sounds are hard to sort without hearing them.
actions: Record a short video of the sound on your phone from where you stand, and note the mode.
Share it with a licensed HVAC pro who works on mini-splits.
If you see sparks or smoke, or smell burning, get out and call 911 from outside.
ms_sound_unsure.avoid: Don’t open the unit or put your ear against it.

ms_smell_room_odor_basic.title: It’s likely blowing back a smell from the room.
ms_smell_room_odor_basic.explanation: Mini-splits can soak up cooking, tobacco smoke, pet, or paint smells and blow them back later.
actions: Ventilate the room if outdoor conditions permit and there is no suspected gas or refrigerant release.
For filter cleaning, start a new check and follow the owner-access gates. Do not open equipment from this result.
If the smell persists, worsens, or cannot be identified, arrange service. Do not wait a week if someone feels unwell.
ms_smell_room_odor_basic.avoid: Don’t spray air freshener or cleaner into the unit.

ms_smell_pro.title: That smell needs a pro.
ms_smell_pro.explanation: A sewage or drain smell can come from a drain problem or other trouble inside the unit.
actions: Turn the unit off with the remote and air out the room.
If anyone feels dizzy, sick, or short of breath, get everyone out and call 911.
Tell the pro what it smells like and when it started.
ms_smell_pro.avoid: Don’t spray anything into the unit or try to clean the drain yourself.

ms_smell_unsure.urgency: Check again later, or call a pro
ms_smell_unsure.title: Hard to tell what the smell is.
ms_smell_unsure.explanation: If you can’t place it, a pro can check it in person.
actions: Note when you notice it, in which mode, and if it’s stronger right after it starts.
Call a licensed HVAC pro who works on mini-splits.
If it starts to smell like burning or gas, get everyone out and call 911 from outside.
ms_smell_unsure.avoid: Don’t open the unit or put your face up to it.

ms_remote_fixed_basic.title: The remote or app is getting through again.
ms_remote_fixed_basic.explanation: The remote or app is responding again based on your answer. Which change helped has not been confirmed.
actions: Keep the remote in the same room, out of direct sun.
If you use an app, check its schedules so it doesn’t undo what you set.
If it stops responding again, start a new check.
ms_remote_fixed_basic.avoid: Don’t press buttons on the indoor unit or change settings on the unit itself.

ms_remote_pro.urgency: Arrange service or a replacement remote
ms_remote_pro.title: The remote or unit isn’t responding.
ms_remote_pro.explanation: If fresh batteries and the steps in your manual don’t help, the remote, the unit’s receiver, or the unit may need service.
actions: Check your manual or the maker’s site for a replacement remote for your model.
If the unit still won’t respond, call a licensed HVAC pro who works on mini-splits.
If a battery leaked, don’t touch it with bare skin. Recycle the old batteries the way your local rules say.
ms_remote_pro.avoid: Don’t open the indoor unit, pry the remote open, or press buttons on the indoor unit.

ms_app_support_info.urgency: Check the app, then its support
ms_app_support_info.title: Use the working remote while checking the app.
ms_app_support_info.explanation: If the remote works, the unit is getting commands. The app depends on your Wi-Fi and the maker’s service.
actions: Use the remote for now.
Check that the app and your Wi-Fi are working, and look for app updates.
Contact the app maker’s support for help with connecting.
Questions about this check: support@secondwrench.co.
ms_app_support_info.avoid: Don’t open the indoor unit or touch its Wi-Fi module or wiring.

ms_feature_fixed_basic.title: You reported improvement after a setting change.
ms_feature_fixed_basic.explanation: Features like Eco, Quiet, Sleep, timers, or a room sensor in the remote can limit how hard it works.
actions: Turn features back on one at a time later if you want them, and see which one makes the difference.
Keep the remote in the room if it has a room sensor.
If it stops keeping up again, start a new check.
ms_feature_fixed_basic.avoid: Don’t change installer or service settings.

ms_louver_sweat_basic.title: The louver may be collecting condensation.
ms_louver_sweat_basic.explanation: In Cool or Dry on humid days, cold air aimed straight down can make the louver and front sweat and drip.
actions: Use the air-direction button on your remote to aim the air more level, the way your manual shows for cooling.
Close windows and doors to the room while it cools.
If water keeps dripping, or drips onto anything that plugs in, start a new check and choose water dripping.
ms_louver_sweat_basic.avoid: Don’t move the louver by hand.

ms_feature_unsure.urgency: Check the manual, or call a pro
ms_feature_unsure.title: Hard to tell which features are on.
ms_feature_unsure.explanation: Remotes and apps name these features differently.
actions: Look at the remote screen and the manual’s list of symbols.
The maker’s support line can tell you how to turn a feature off for your model.
If it still won’t keep up, call a licensed HVAC pro who works on mini-splits.
Questions about this check: support@secondwrench.co.
ms_feature_unsure.avoid: Don’t press buttons on the indoor unit or open installer menus.

ms_musty_dryout_basic.title: Try drying out the unit.
ms_musty_dryout_basic.explanation: Moisture left inside after cooling can smell musty, even when the part you can see looks clean.
actions: Refit only fully dry filters and close their cover before operation. Do not run with filters removed.

Only if the exact owner’s manual permits Fan or a remote self-dry function, no hazard or code is present, and nobody needs heating or cooling, follow those owner instructions. Do not select a freeze-cleaning function.
For persistent odor or visible growth, arrange professional cleaning. Do not spray or brush inside the unit.
ms_musty_dryout_basic.avoid: Don’t spray cleaner, bleach, or anything else into the unit.

ms_head_inside_damage_pro.title: Something inside the unit is damaged or loose.
ms_head_inside_damage_pro.explanation: Bent fins, loose parts, or loose wires inside need a pro.
actions: Don’t touch anything inside. Close the filter cover only if it closes easily without touching anything behind it, and leave the unit off with the remote.
Call a licensed HVAC pro who works on mini-splits, and tell them what you saw.
If you see sparks or smoke, or smell burning, get out and call 911 from outside.
ms_head_inside_damage_pro.avoid: Don’t touch, straighten, or push anything back inside the unit.

ms_condensate_outside_normal_basic.title: That can match normal condensate drainage.
ms_condensate_outside_normal_basic.explanation: When it cools or dries the air, the water it removes drains outside. On dry days there may be little or none.
actions: Keep the drip area clear of things that could block it.
If water ever shows up at or under the indoor unit, start a new check and choose water dripping.
ms_condensate_outside_normal_basic.avoid: Don’t move, dig at, or push anything into the drain hose.

ms_condensate_outlet_pro.title: The drain outlet needs a pro.
ms_condensate_outlet_pro.explanation: A drain hose that’s damaged or buried, or that drips where people walk or near the foundation, can back up into the indoor unit or make an icy spot.
actions: Keep people off any icy patch. If you normally use ice melt on that walkway, keep it off the drain hose and the outdoor unit.
Call a licensed HVAC pro to reroute or repair the drain outlet.
If water shows up at the indoor unit, start a new check and choose water dripping.
ms_condensate_outlet_pro.avoid: Don’t move, cut, dig at, or push anything into the drain hose.

ms_code_status_basic.title: Your manual says that’s a normal status.
ms_code_status_basic.explanation: Some lights and codes mean the unit is defrosting, reminding you to clean the filters, or showing a timer was reset.
actions: Record the exact status and its meaning in your matching manual. A status message does not establish normal heating or cooling.

A filter reminder does not authorize opening the unit from this result. Use the separate filter check with its manual, access, power-isolation, and heating-or-cooling pause questions, or ask a professional.
For a timer, use only ordinary remote instructions in the exact owner’s manual. Do not clear a stored fault or enter a service menu.
If the equipment is not providing needed heating or cooling, arrange service.
ms_code_status_basic.avoid: Don’t open the unit, clear codes or error history from any menu, or reset breakers.

ms_error_code_serious_pro.title: That code is a pro job.
ms_error_code_serious_pro.explanation: Codes about refrigerant, the compressor, high pressure, or overheating usually mean the unit stopped itself to protect its parts. A pro needs to find out why.
actions: Turn it off with the remote and leave it off.
Give the pro the code, what your manual says it means, and the model.

If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first. Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
ms_error_code_serious_pro.avoid: Don’t turn it off and on again to clear the code, don’t clear its history, and don’t reset breakers.

ms_restart_cleared_basic.title: The code cleared after one restart.
ms_restart_cleared_basic.explanation: You reported that the unit is running and the code cleared. The cause of the code has not been confirmed.
actions: Keep the code and date you wrote down.
If the same code shows again, don’t restart it again. Call a licensed HVAC pro and tell them the code.
ms_restart_cleared_basic.avoid: Don’t restart it again if the code returns.

ms_error_code_returned_pro.title: The code came back. Leave it for a pro.
ms_error_code_returned_pro.explanation: Repeated shutdown or a returning code needs professional investigation. A restart does not establish the cause.
actions: Turn it off with the remote and leave it off.
Give the pro the code, what your manual says, and when it came back.

If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first. Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
ms_error_code_returned_pro.avoid: Don’t restart it again, and don’t reset breakers.

ms_cold_weather_stop.title: Leave this one to a pro for now.
ms_cold_weather_stop.explanation: Second Wrench doesn’t guide these changes when it’s 40 °F (4 °C) or colder outside, or will be in the next few days. That’s our own cautious cutoff, not a rating for your equipment. If anyone at home is an infant, elderly, or medically fragile, leave these to a professional.
actions: Leave the unit running in Heat if it’s heating at all.
Call a licensed HVAC pro who works on mini-splits.
If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first.

If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first. Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
ms_cold_weather_stop.avoid: Don’t turn units off or restart them to test them for now.

ms_ask_installer.title: Check with your installer first.
ms_ask_installer.explanation: If your system or this part was installed recently, check with your installer first. Some warranties and installer agreements expect them to make changes. Changing things yourself may affect what they’ll cover.
actions: Call the company that installed it. Give them the code and what you saw.
If you can’t reach them, call a licensed HVAC pro who works on mini-splits.
ms_ask_installer.avoid: Don’t make changes until your installer says it’s OK.

ms_zone_mode_match_basic.urgency: Keep the units on one mode
ms_zone_mode_match_basic.title: You reported improvement after matching the modes.
ms_zone_mode_match_basic.explanation: The outdoor unit can’t heat one room and cool another at the same time. With every indoor unit on the same mode, it can serve them all.
actions: Keep every indoor unit on the same mode, Heat or Cool, while the system is in use.
Leave Auto off for now. If you use Auto again, watch whether the units end up on different modes.
If the problem comes back with every unit on one mode, start a new check.
ms_zone_mode_match_basic.avoid: Don’t change addresses, priority, or settings on the outdoor unit.

ms_zone_control_pro.title: Your installer or a pro can set the controls.
ms_zone_control_pro.explanation: Some systems lock modes or use a central control. Changing that is a job for your installer or a licensed HVAC professional.
actions: Leave the units you can’t change as they are.
Call your installer or a licensed HVAC pro who works on mini-splits. Tell them which units are on which mode and what each one shows.
ms_zone_control_pro.avoid: Don’t try to unlock settings, enter an access code, or change settings on the outdoor unit.

ms_zone_unsure.title: The mode check needs a clearer answer.
ms_zone_unsure.explanation: It’s fine not to know. Leave the units on one mode for now.
actions: Do not guess at controls or switch off rooms to test them.
Call a professional with the modes and displays you could read.
ms_zone_unsure.avoid: Don’t change settings on the outdoor unit, and don’t climb to check an indoor unit.

ms_filter_pause_pro.title: Postpone filter cleaning until the home can manage without this unit
ms_filter_pause_pro.explanation: Do not start a cleaning task that may leave needed heating or cooling unavailable while filters dry.
actions: Leave the required filters and their cover in place. Do not run with filters removed.
Ask a licensed HVAC professional to plan the filter service around the home’s heating or cooling needs.
If the home is becoming too cold or hot, arrange help and get anyone at risk to a place with suitable heating or cooling first.
ms_filter_pause_pro.avoid: Do not remove filters before you can leave the unit Off through the full cleaning and drying time.

bl.tstat.call.title: Is the thermostat calling for heat?
bl.tstat.call.body:
Look at the thermostat you already use. Don’t take it off the wall.

1. Mode is Heat.
2. Setpoint is a few degrees above the room temperature.

Some thermostats wait a few minutes before starting heat. Radiators and floors can take a while to warm up.

bl_gas_smell.title: Leave the house now.
bl_gas_smell.explanation: A gas smell comes before anything else.
actions: Get everyone, and pets, out now.
Don’t touch light switches, the thermostat, phones, or anything that could spark while you’re inside.
Don’t try to find the leak.
From outside or a neighbor’s, call the gas utility’s emergency line or 911.
Don’t go back in until emergency responders say you may return.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_gas_smell.avoid: Don’t try to shut off the gas yourself.

bl_co_alarm.title: Get everyone out to fresh air now.
bl_co_alarm.explanation: A CO alarm or these symptoms can mean carbon monoxide. You can’t see or smell it.
actions: Get everyone, and pets, outside to fresh air now.
From outside, call 911 or the fire department.
Don’t go back in until responders say you may return.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_co_alarm.avoid: Don’t silence the alarm and stay inside, and don’t open windows instead of leaving.

bl_soot_scorch.urgency: Stop · keep away from the boiler
bl_soot_scorch.title: Stop using the boiler.
bl_soot_scorch.explanation: These signs can mean unsafe burning and carbon monoxide.
actions: For a gas smell, a CO alarm, smoke, or possible CO illness, get everyone outside immediately and call 911 or the gas utility from outside. Do not operate a switch on the way out. Only when none of those signs is present, use only a clearly identified external boiler emergency shutoff that you can reach from dry ground without going near hot water, steam, or the boiler. Do not open a cover or operate a gas or water valve. If you cannot do that, move away and call for emergency help. A room thermostat set to Off may not stop a boiler that also serves other zones or hot water.
If you smell gas, a CO alarm sounds, or anyone feels sick, get everyone out and call 911 from outside.
Call a licensed heating professional before using the boiler again.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_soot_scorch.avoid: Don’t open, reset, or restart the boiler.

bl_burning_sparks.title: Get away from the boiler and call 911.
bl_burning_sparks.explanation: A burning or electrical smell, smoke, or sparks can mean a fire is starting.
actions: Get everyone, and pets, out.
Call 911 from outside.
Don’t go back in until responders say you may return.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_burning_sparks.avoid: Don’t stay to troubleshoot, open the boiler, or flip switches or breakers.

bl_water_steam_release.title: Stay back from the spray.
bl_water_steam_release.explanation: Escaping hot water or steam can scald and can mean the boiler is too hot or over pressure.
actions: For a gas smell, a CO alarm, smoke, or possible CO illness, get everyone outside immediately and call 911 or the gas utility from outside. Do not operate a switch on the way out. Only when none of those signs is present, use only a clearly identified external boiler emergency shutoff that you can reach from dry ground without going near hot water, steam, or the boiler. Do not open a cover or operate a gas or water valve. If you cannot do that, move away and call for emergency help. A room thermostat set to Off may not stop a boiler that also serves other zones or hot water.
Keep everyone, and pets, away.
Call a licensed heating professional now. If anyone is burned, call 911.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_water_steam_release.avoid: Don’t touch, cap, or plug the valve or pipe, or close any valves.

bl_water_electrical.title: Stay clear of the water and the boiler.
bl_water_electrical.explanation: Water near wiring can shock, and a boiler that has been under water needs its controls checked before it runs.
actions: Stay out of standing water.

Switch power off only at a known breaker or disconnect you can reach from dry ground, without touching water or going near the affected equipment. Use the handle only; do not remove covers. Otherwise, move away and call 911 from outside if there is immediate danger.
Call a licensed heating professional. If water is rising or you see sparks, get out and call 911.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_water_electrical.avoid: Don’t touch the boiler, its switch, or cords while there’s water near them.

bl_pressure_relief_stop.urgency: Turn the heat off · call now
bl_pressure_relief_stop.title: Stay back and call for urgent boiler service.
bl_pressure_relief_stop.explanation: At this pressure the relief valve can open and release scalding water or steam.
actions: For a gas smell, a CO alarm, smoke, or possible CO illness, get everyone outside immediately and call 911 or the gas utility from outside. Do not operate a switch on the way out. Only when none of those signs is present, use only a clearly identified external boiler emergency shutoff that you can reach from dry ground without going near hot water, steam, or the boiler. Do not open a cover or operate a gas or water valve. If you cannot do that, move away and call for emergency help. A room thermostat set to Off may not stop a boiler that also serves other zones or hot water.
Keep everyone away from the relief valve pipe.
Call a licensed heating professional now. Tell them the gauge reading.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_pressure_relief_stop.avoid: Don’t drain water, touch the relief valve, or try to lower the pressure yourself.

bl_steam_glass_empty.title: Don’t add water.
bl_steam_glass_empty.explanation: An empty or unreadable steam-boiler sight glass may mean dangerously low water. Stop using the boiler and call for urgent service. Do not add water, even after it cools.
actions: Keep everyone away from the boiler.

Only if there is no gas smell, smoke, spray, or water near electrical parts, use the clearly identified external boiler emergency shutoff if you can reach it from dry ground without going near the boiler. Do not open any cover or operate a gas or water valve.
If you cannot shut it down without approaching a hazard, leave the area and call the fire department or 911 from outside. Otherwise, call a licensed heating professional for urgent service now.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_steam_glass_empty.avoid: Don’t add water, drain water, open valves, press resets, or restart the boiler.

bl_bang_puffback.title: Stop using the boiler.
