actions: For a gas smell, a CO alarm, smoke, or possible CO illness, get everyone outside immediately and call 911 or the gas utility from outside. Do not operate a switch on the way out. Only when none of those signs is present, use only a clearly identified external boiler emergency shutoff that you can reach from dry ground without going near hot water, steam, or the boiler. Do not open a cover or operate a gas or water valve. If you cannot do that, move away and call for emergency help. A room thermostat set to Off may not stop a boiler that also serves other zones or hot water.
Call a licensed heating professional, or your oil company if you have oil heat.
If you smell gas or a CO alarm sounds, get everyone out and call 911 from outside.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_bang_puffback.avoid: Don’t open the boiler, press reset buttons, or try to relight anything.

bl_cold_exposure.urgency: Warm them now · call 911 if needed
bl_cold_exposure.title: Get the person at risk warm now.
bl_cold_exposure.explanation: Cold can harm babies, older adults, and people with medical needs quickly.
actions: Move them to a warm place, like a neighbor, relative, or warming center.
If they are confused, very drowsy, or hard to wake, call 911.
Then call a licensed heating professional for emergency service.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_cold_exposure.avoid: Don’t wait at home in the cold for the boiler to come back.

bl_gate_unsure.title: Stop here. Not sure means don’t continue.
bl_gate_unsure.explanation: If you can’t rule out a hazard, stop the check.
actions: Do not approach the boiler to investigate an uncertain hazard.
For a possible gas smell, CO alarm, smoke, or illness, get everyone outside and call for emergency help.
Otherwise stay away and call a licensed heating professional for guidance on shutdown. A thermostat set to Off may not stop other heating zones or hot-water operation.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_gate_unsure.avoid: Don’t keep checking the boiler to find out.

bl_fragile_cold_pro.title: Call for emergency heating service now.
bl_fragile_cold_pro.explanation: With someone fragile at home in cold weather, no heat needs a pro now.
actions: Keep them warm: layers, one warm room, or a neighbor, relative, or warming center.
Call a licensed heating professional for emergency service now. Tell them who is home.
If anyone is confused, very drowsy, or hard to wake, call 911.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_fragile_cold_pro.avoid: Don’t try resets or other boiler steps while you wait.

bl_tstat_set_heat_basic.title: Set the thermostat to call for heat.
bl_tstat_set_heat_basic.explanation: This thermostat controls a heating zone. A boiler may also run for other zones or to maintain domestic hot water; this one thermostat does not control every boiler function.
actions: For this room or zone, select Heat and set the temperature a little above the displayed room temperature.
Radiators and floors respond slowly. If the home is getting cold or someone is at risk, arrange heat and service now instead of waiting.
If heat does not begin returning, call a licensed heating professional. Record what the thermostat and boiler display show.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_tstat_set_heat_basic.avoid: Don’t take the thermostat off the wall.

bl_emitters_cleared_basic.title: Give the heat room to move.
bl_emitters_cleared_basic.explanation: Baseboard and radiators heat the room by letting air flow over and around them.
actions: Keep furniture and curtains outside the clearance specified in the emitter’s owner’s manual. Do not remove covers or touch hot surfaces.
If the rooms are falling behind, arrange service; do not delay help for a vulnerable person.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_emitters_cleared_basic.avoid: Don’t remove baseboard covers or open radiator valves.

bl_batteries_display_back.title: Now set it to call for heat.
bl_batteries_display_back.explanation: New batteries brought the thermostat screen back.
actions: Check the normal heating mode and setpoint on the restored display.
If needed heat does not return promptly, arrange service. A restored display does not prove the boiler works.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_batteries_display_back.avoid: Don’t take the thermostat off the wall.

bl_pressure_in_range_basic.title: Record the reading and compare with your manual.
bl_pressure_in_range_basic.explanation: A gauge reading alone cannot confirm that the boiler is operating properly. Steam and hot-water boilers use different ranges, and the installation matters.
actions: Write down the reading, its units, and whether the boiler was running.
Use the range in your exact owner’s manual. If you cannot confirm it, or pressure changes unexpectedly, call a licensed heating professional.
Keep away from any leaking relief valve or discharge pipe.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_pressure_in_range_basic.avoid: Don’t add or drain water to change the reading.

bl_tstat_unsure.title: Let’s get the thermostat settings first.
bl_tstat_unsure.explanation: This check needs to know whether the thermostat is asking for heat.
actions: Look at the thermostat’s mode and setpoint, or check its manual.
Then start this check again.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_tstat_unsure.avoid: Don’t take the thermostat off the wall.

bl_type_unconfirmed.title: We couldn’t confirm the boiler type.
bl_type_unconfirmed.explanation: The checks differ for hot-water and steam boilers.
actions: Look for the maker’s label you can read without opening anything, or a manual or past service invoice.
Or call a licensed heating professional.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_type_unconfirmed.avoid: Don’t remove panels or climb to read a label.

bl_pressure_unsure.title: We couldn’t get a gauge reading.
bl_pressure_unsure.explanation: The pressure check needs a reading you can see without opening anything.
actions: Check the manual for where the gauge is.
Or call a licensed heating professional and tell them what you saw.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_pressure_unsure.avoid: Don’t open panels or touch valves to find it.

bl_switch_off_pro.title: A switch that is off or a tripped breaker is a job for a pro.
bl_switch_off_pro.explanation: It may have been turned off on purpose, so ask a pro before it goes back on.
actions: Leave the breaker and the boiler switch as they are, and call a licensed heating professional or electrician.
If you smell burning or see smoke, get people away and call 911 from outside.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_switch_off_pro.avoid: Don’t reset breakers, turn the boiler switch on, or open the boiler.

bl_vent_blocked.urgency: Turn the heat off · call a pro
bl_vent_blocked.title: Stop using the boiler and call a professional.
bl_vent_blocked.explanation: A blocked vent can stop the boiler or push exhaust and carbon monoxide back inside.
actions: For a gas smell, a CO alarm, smoke, or possible CO illness, get everyone outside immediately and call 911 or the gas utility from outside. Do not operate a switch on the way out. Only when none of those signs is present, use only a clearly identified external boiler emergency shutoff that you can reach from dry ground without going near hot water, steam, or the boiler. Do not open a cover or operate a gas or water valve. If you cannot do that, move away and call for emergency help. A room thermostat set to Off may not stop a boiler that also serves other zones or hot water.
Call a licensed heating professional, and tell them what blocks the pipe.
If a CO alarm sounds or anyone feels sick, get everyone out and call 911 from outside.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_vent_blocked.avoid: Don’t chip ice, climb, or reset the boiler.

bl_relief_weep_pro.title: Call a licensed heating professional soon.
bl_relief_weep_pro.explanation: A dripping relief valve needs a professional to check pressure, temperature, the valve, and the expansion tank. The drip alone does not identify the cause.
actions: Stay clear of the discharge pipe and keep its outlet unobstructed.
Record a gauge reading only if you can already see it without approaching the leak.
Call a licensed heating professional today. For spraying hot water or steam, stay back and seek urgent help.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_relief_weep_pro.avoid: Don’t cap, plug, or lift the valve’s lever.

bl_ask_installer.title: Ask your installer first.
bl_ask_installer.explanation: Your installer may want to make this change to keep coverage in place.
actions: Call your installer and tell them what you noticed.
If you can’t reach them, call a licensed heating professional.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_ask_installer.avoid: Don’t open the boiler or change other settings.

bl_call_pro.title: Call a licensed heating professional.
bl_call_pro.explanation: The cause has not been confirmed. The next checks need a licensed heating professional.
actions: Call a licensed heating professional and describe the observations and remaining unknowns.
If a new smell, alarm, smoke, leak, steam, or bang appears, use Stop / get help immediately.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_call_pro.avoid: Don’t press reset buttons again, restart, add water, or open panels.

bl_cold_home_urgent.title: Arrange urgent heating help now
bl_cold_home_urgent.explanation: The home is losing heat, pipes may be at risk, or the risk to people is uncertain. Do not wait through more equipment checks.
actions: Get anyone who needs warmth to a warm place first. Bring pets somewhere warm too.
Call a licensed heating professional for urgent service. For suspected frozen plumbing, also call a plumber; do not thaw it yourself.
For confusion, severe drowsiness, or difficulty waking someone, call 911.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
bl_cold_home_urgent.avoid: Do not use equipment checks or repeated restarts to delay getting warmth and help.

bl_refrigerant_alarm.title: Leave the affected area
bl_refrigerant_alarm.explanation: A refrigerant leak alarm needs people out of the affected area. This boiler check does not identify the refrigerant or the cause.
actions: Move people out of the affected area to fresh air without operating switches or creating ignition sources.
Call a licensed HVAC professional with EPA 608 capability from outside the affected area and follow the equipment’s alarm instructions. For breathing trouble or immediate danger, call 911.
Do not DIY-seal a leak or add refrigerant.
bl_refrigerant_alarm.avoid: Do not turn off a mitigation blower, cycle power, bypass a sensor, use flames, or open refrigerant lines.

no_fire_after_basics: The boiler stays cool while the thermostat calls for heat.
Tell them: boiler stays cool on a heat call.
circulation_after_basics: The boiler gets hot, but the heat isn’t reaching the rooms.
Tell them: boiler hot, rooms cold, which zones.
steam_distribution_after_basics: Steam radiators stay cold or heat unevenly.
Tell them: which radiators stay cold, any noises.
thermostat_control_issue: The thermostat won’t take Heat or a new setpoint.
Tell them: the thermostat model and what it does.
blank_tstat_after_basics: The thermostat screen is still blank after new batteries.
Tell them: blank screen after new batteries.
blank_tstat_no_batteries: The thermostat is blank and has no batteries.
Tell them: blank thermostat, no batteries.
tstat_inaccessible: The thermostat batteries couldn’t be reached without opening anything.
Tell them: the thermostat screen is blank.
display_dark: The boiler display is dark with the switches on.
Tell them: display dark, switches looked on.
boiler_inaccessible: The boiler couldn’t be reached without opening anything.
Tell them: what blocks the way.
low_pressure: The gauge reads low. That can stop the boiler and can mean a leak.
Tell them: the reading and any code.
pressure_high: The gauge reads high, which can point to an expansion tank problem.
Tell them: the reading, hot or cold.
code_pressure_ok: The gauge is in the usual range, so the code points somewhere else.
Tell them: the exact code and the reading.
oil_lockout: An oil boiler lockout needs a pro. This guide doesn’t walk oil resets.
Tell them: the code or light, and oil level.
overheat_code: The boiler shut down on high temperature.
Tell them: the code and the gauge reading.
vent_code_after_look: The code points to the vent or drain, but nothing outside looks blocked.
Tell them: the code; vents looked clear.
other_code: The code points to a part inside the boiler.
Tell them: the exact code, brand, and model.
code_unknown: A pro can look up the code for your model.
Tell them: the exact code, brand, and model.
reset_already_used: It was already reset once. Another reset could hide a real fault.
Tell them: the code and the earlier reset.
reset_failed: The same code came back after one reset. A safety device is doing its job.
Tell them: the code, before and after the reset.
reset_new_code: A new code showed up after one reset.
Tell them: both codes, in order.
reset_not_on_model: We only show resets from owner’s manuals we’ve checked.
Tell them: the exact code, brand, and model.
notice_declined: You chose a pro instead of the homeowner step. That’s always fine.
Tell them: what you saw so far.
steam_low_water: The steam boiler is low on water. Needing water often can mean a leak.
Tell them: the level and how often.
steam_water_level: The steam water level is too high or unsteady.
Tell them: full or jumping level, any banging.
steam_glass_unreadable: The steam water level couldn’t be seen.
Tell them: you couldn’t see the level.
condensate_issue: The drain tube looks blocked, frozen, or off its drain.
Tell them: what the drain tube looks like.
vent_inaccessible: The vent pipes couldn’t be seen from the ground.
Tell them: where the vents are.
air_in_system: Gurgling or cold tops usually mean air in the system.
Tell them: which radiators or zones.
air_after_bleed: Air was let out, but it’s still cold or gurgling.
Tell them: which vents, and the gauge before and after.
pressure_low_after_bleed: The pressure dropped after air was let out. The system may need water a pro adds.
Tell them: the gauge before and after.
guard_blocked: Air in the system is likely. With the cold or who’s at home, we leave letting air out to a pro.
Tell them: which radiators, and who’s at home.

heat: One zone stays cold with its thermostat calling.
Tell them: which zone and its thermostat.
dhw: The tank stays cold while the boiler runs.
Tell them: boiler hot, tank cold.

heat: The zone valve shows power, but the zone stays cold.
Tell them: valve light on steady, zone cold.
dhw: The tank’s zone valve shows power, but the tank stays cold.
Tell them: valve light on steady, tank cold.

heat: The zone valve light is off, so it may not be getting the call.
Tell them: valve light off with the thermostat calling.
dhw: The tank’s zone valve light is off, so it may not be getting the call.
Tell them: valve light off with a hot tap running.

heat: The zone valve light shows a fault pattern.
Tell them: how the light blinks, and which zone.
dhw: The tank’s zone valve light shows a fault pattern.
Tell them: how the light blinks.

indirect_no_call: The boiler doesn’t start when the tank calls.
Tell them: tank cold, boiler doesn’t start, the tank dial reading.
indirect_unclear: It’s not clear what the boiler does when the tank calls.
Tell them: what the water heater check found.
tankless_coil: Hot water comes from a coil inside the boiler. That’s a pro check.
Tell them: no hot water, coil in the boiler.
coil_source_unclear: It’s not clear what heats the water for the coil.
Tell them: hot-water coil in the ducts, no heat.
coil_loop_wh_source: The water heater makes hot water, but it isn’t reaching the coil.
Tell them: hot taps work, coil pipe cool.
rooms_unclear: It’s not clear which rooms are short on heat.
Tell them: which rooms feel cold, and when.
steam_hammer: Banging in steam pipes often comes from water sitting in them.
Tell them: which pipes bang, and when.
kettling: Kettle sounds can mean deposits or low flow in the boiler.
Tell them: the sound and when it happens.
circulator_noise: Grinding or squealing near the boiler needs a pro.
Tell them: where the noise is.
noise_other: This guide doesn’t diagnose that sound.
Tell them: the sound and when it happens.
condensate_leak: Water around the drain tube can mean a blocked or leaking drain.
Tell them: where the water is.
emitter_leak: A leak at a radiator, valve, or vent needs a pro.
boiler_leak: Water from the boiler or nearby pipes needs a pro soon.
Tell them: where, and how much.
diy_not_offered: Fixes inside the boiler are work for a licensed pro.
Tell them: what you wanted to fix.

step.what: Reading the light changes nothing on the furnace.
step.caution: Removing the door or cutting power can erase the stored code on some brands.
step.source: Carrier 58-3T, service information label; checked October 12, 2026. Codes differ by model and control.
steps: Look through an existing window or at an already-visible display without opening a cover.
Watch a complete repeating pattern. Record its colors, long and short flashes, or displayed characters. A phone video may help.
step.watch: Do not delay an urgent heating-service call to collect a code.
step.stop: Stop if you smell gas or burning, hear a CO alarm, or see water near wires.
step.undo: If you’re not sure what you changed, put back what you wrote down. If you can’t, leave it and call a licensed HVAC professional. Don’t guess. For a hazard, follow the emergency instructions instead of going back to equipment.
step.locked: Do not change gas valves, burner controls, wiring, blower or heat-stage setup, limits, rollout or pressure switches, freezestats, or stored error history. Do not enter installer passwords or access codes.

fn_gas_smell.title: Leave the house now.
fn_gas_smell.explanation: A gas smell comes before anything else.
actions: Get everyone, and pets, out now.
Don't touch light switches, the thermostat, phones, or anything that could spark while you're inside.
Don't try to find the leak.
From outside or a neighbor's, call the gas utility's emergency line or 911.
Don't go back in until they say you can go back in.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_gas_smell.avoid: Don't try to shut off the gas yourself.

fn_co_alarm.title: Get everyone outside to fresh air now.
fn_co_alarm.body:
1. Get everyone, including pets, out of the house now. Don't stop to open windows or look for the problem.
2. From outside, call 911 or your fire department. If anyone is very sleepy, confused, vomiting, has chest pain, or passes out, call 911 right away.
3. Don't go back inside until the fire department or your gas utility says it's OK.
4. Anyone with symptoms should get checked by a doctor, even if they feel better outside. Tell them you may have been exposed to carbon monoxide.
5. In an emergency, call 911 first. For questions about symptoms when it isn't an emergency, call Poison Control: U.S. 1-800-222-1222. Canada 1-844-POISON-X (1-844-764-7669). Quebec 1-800-463-5060. Nunavut: your local health centre.
6. Before using the heat again, have a licensed HVAC professional check the system.
fn_co_alarm.footer: Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.

5. In an emergency, call 911 first. For questions about symptoms when it isn't an emergency, call Poison Control: U.S. 1-800-222-1222. Canada 1-844-POISON-X (1-844-764-7669). Quebec 1-800-463-5060. Nunavut: your local health centre.
6. Before using the heat again, have a licensed HVAC professional check the system.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_co_alarm.avoid: Don't go back inside to troubleshoot, open windows, or silence the alarm.

fn_rollout_soot.urgency: Stop · keep away from the furnace
fn_rollout_soot.title: Stop using the furnace.
fn_rollout_soot.explanation: Soot, scorch marks, or flame outside the burner can mean unsafe burning and carbon monoxide.
actions: If you're at the thermostat and smell no gas, set it to Off.
If you smell gas, a CO alarm sounds, or anyone feels sick, get everyone out and call 911 from outside.
Call a licensed HVAC pro before using the furnace again.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_rollout_soot.avoid: Don't open, reset, or restart the furnace.

fn_burning_sparks.title: Stop. Treat this as a fire risk.
fn_burning_sparks.explanation: Smoke, sparks, or a burning-plastic or electrical smell can't be checked from here.
actions: Get everyone away from the furnace. If there's smoke or fire, leave and call 911 from outside.
Don't use the furnace until a licensed HVAC pro checks it.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_burning_sparks.avoid: Don't stay to troubleshoot, open the furnace, or flip switches or breakers.

fn_cold_exposure.urgency: Get warm now · call 911 if needed
fn_cold_exposure.title: Get the person warm first.
fn_cold_exposure.explanation: Someone at risk from the cold matters more than the furnace.
actions: If anyone is confused, very drowsy, or hard to wake, call 911 now.
Otherwise, get them somewhere warm: a neighbor, family, or a warming center.
Add blankets and dry layers in the meantime.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
Call a licensed HVAC pro for the furnace once everyone is warm.
fn_cold_exposure.avoid: Don't wait on a furnace repair to get someone warm.

fn_flame_abnormal.title: Stop using the furnace and call a pro.
fn_flame_abnormal.explanation: A yellow or orange flame can mean the furnace isn't burning cleanly. That can make carbon monoxide.
actions: Set the thermostat to Off.
Don't use the furnace until a licensed HVAC pro checks it.
Make sure your CO alarms work. If one sounds or anyone feels sick, get everyone out and call 911 from outside.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_flame_abnormal.avoid: Don't open the furnace or go look at the flame again.

fn_ignition_bang.title: Stop using the furnace and call a pro.
fn_ignition_bang.explanation: A bang when it starts can mean gas is building up before it lights.
actions: Set the thermostat to Off.
Don't keep restarting it to see if it happens again.
Call a licensed HVAC pro. If you smell gas, leave and call from outside.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_ignition_bang.avoid: Don't open the furnace, press reset buttons, or try to relight anything.

fn_gate_unsure.title: Not sure is a good reason to stop.
fn_gate_unsure.explanation: You don't need to check the furnace to answer. Stopping is the right stop.
actions: If you smell gas or a CO alarm sounds, get everyone out and call 911 from outside.
If not, set the thermostat to Off if you're already there, and call a licensed HVAC pro.
Tell them what you noticed.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_gate_unsure.avoid: Don't open the furnace or look at the flame to find out.

fn_hazard_now.title: A new hazard ends this check.
actions: Gas smell: leave now. Don't touch switches, phones, or anything that could spark. From outside, call the gas utility or 911.
CO alarm or feeling sick: get everyone and pets out to fresh air. Call 911 from outside.
Smoke, sparks, or burning smell: get away and call 911 from outside.

If a refrigerant leak alarm is going off, move people out of the affected area to fresh air without operating switches or creating ignition sources. Don’t reset the alarm, cycle power, or turn off a blower that’s running. Call a licensed HVAC professional from outside the affected area, and for breathing trouble or immediate danger, call 911.
Don't go back in until responders say you can go back in.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.

fn_tstat_set_heat_basic.title: Set Heat and a higher setpoint.
fn_tstat_set_heat_basic.explanation: The thermostat wasn't asking for heat. That's an easy fix.
actions: Set the mode to Heat.
Raise the setpoint a few degrees above the room temperature. Fan on Auto.
Still no heat after 10 minutes? Start a new check and answer that heat still won't come on.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_tstat_set_heat_basic.avoid: Don't take the thermostat off the wall or change wiring or installer settings.

fn_fan_auto_basic.title: Set the fan to Auto.
fn_fan_auto_basic.explanation: With the fan on On, the blower runs between heating cycles and moves room-temperature air. That can feel cold.
actions: Set the fan to Auto. Leave the mode on Heat.
Wait for the next heating cycle. The air should feel warm while the heat runs.
Still cool air while the heat runs? Start a new check and pick Furnace.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_fan_auto_basic.avoid: Don't change wiring or installer settings.

fn_tstat_unsure.title: Read the thermostat, then try again.
fn_tstat_unsure.explanation: The next step depends on the mode and setpoint.
actions: Read the mode, setpoint, and fan setting on the screen, or check the thermostat manual.
Start a new check when you can.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_tstat_unsure.avoid: Don't take the thermostat off the wall or open the furnace to find out.

fn_filter_replace_basic.title: The filter looks dirty or clogged.
fn_filter_replace_basic.explanation: A clogged filter chokes airflow, and a furnace can shut itself off.
actions: Put in the right size and type. Match the airflow arrow.
Put any filter door or cover back fully. Don't run the furnace with it off.
Set Heat and retest in 15 to 30 minutes. No better? Call a licensed HVAC pro.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_filter_replace_basic.avoid: Don't run it without a filter or reach into the blower.

fn_filter_missing_basic.title: No filter is installed.
fn_filter_missing_basic.explanation: Running without a filter lets dust build up inside the furnace.
actions: Install the right size and type. Match the airflow arrow.
Put any filter door or cover back fully before running heat.
Set Heat and retest in 15 to 30 minutes. No better? Call a licensed HVAC pro.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_filter_missing_basic.avoid: Don't guess the size, stack filters, or force a fit.

fn_batteries_display_back.title: Fresh batteries brought the screen back.
fn_batteries_display_back.explanation: That doesn't prove the rest of the system is fine.
actions: If no warning signs have appeared, restore the normal Heat setting, the recorded heating setpoint, and the recorded fan setting. Do not change a setting you cannot identify.
Allow at least five minutes for a normal thermostat delay, or the longer delay in your exact manual, only while the home has enough heat and nobody is at risk.
If useful heat does not return, arrange service. A restored display does not prove the equipment works.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_batteries_display_back.avoid: Don't pull thermostat wires or open the furnace.

fn_returns_supplies_cleared.title: A blocked vent was cleared, and airflow's better.
fn_returns_supplies_cleared.explanation: Blocked returns and closed registers can leave rooms short on heat.
actions: Keep the existing returns and registers clear of furniture, rugs, and curtains.
Observe only while the home has enough heat and nobody is at risk. If rooms remain short on heat, call a licensed HVAC professional.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_returns_supplies_cleared.avoid: Don't cut ducts, open a chase, or remove the blower panel.

fn_out_of_scope_equipment.title: This guide doesn't cover that heating system yet.
fn_out_of_scope_equipment.explanation: This check covers gas, oil, and electric furnaces and hot-water air handlers. Wood, coal, pellet, wall and floor heaters, and rooftop equipment need a professional familiar with that equipment.
actions: Call a licensed pro who works on your type of system.
Fuel-burning heat needs working CO alarms. If one sounds, get everyone out and call 911 from outside.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_out_of_scope_equipment.avoid: Don't open the equipment or relight anything to find out what's wrong.

fn_mini_split_oos.title: A ductless mini-split has its own check.
fn_mini_split_oos.explanation: This furnace check is for ducted furnaces. Cooling problems on one indoor unit start on the Something else screen.
actions: Go back home, press Start, and choose “Something else: mini-split, geothermal, thermostat, other”, then “Ductless mini-split”.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_mini_split_oos.avoid: Don't remove covers to identify the equipment.

fn_system_unconfirmed.title: We need to know the furnace type.
fn_system_unconfirmed.explanation: Gas and electric furnaces need different checks.
actions: Check the manual, a label you can read without opening anything, or ask someone who knows the system.
Start a new check when you know. If you can't tell, call a licensed HVAC pro.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_system_unconfirmed.avoid: Don't remove panels or climb to read a label.

fn_call_pro.title: Call a licensed HVAC pro.
fn_call_pro.explanation: The cause has not been confirmed. Share the observations you actually made, and any checks you could not complete, with a licensed HVAC professional.
actions: Call a licensed HVAC professional and share the service note below.
Use Stop / get help for a new smell, alarm, smoke, water at electrical parts, or cold exposure.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_call_pro.avoid: Don't press reset buttons, keep restarting, open panels, or relight anything.

fn_water_electrical.title: Don't touch the furnace or stand in the water.
fn_water_electrical.explanation: Water is at or near the furnace's electrical parts.
actions: Don't touch the furnace, any switch, or the breaker panel, and don't stand in the water.
Leave the area, keep others and pets away, and call a licensed HVAC pro or an electrician.
If you see sparks, smoke, or smell burning, get out and call 911 from outside.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_water_electrical.avoid: Don't touch the furnace, any switch, or the breaker panel.

fn_vent_high_pro.title: Leave high vents to a pro
fn_vent_high_pro.explanation: The furnace pipes are too high to reach from dry, level ground.
actions: Call a licensed HVAC pro and say snow or ice may be blocking the furnace vent.
Keep CO alarms on, and leave if one sounds.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_vent_high_pro.avoid: Don't use a ladder or go on the roof.

fn_vent_unsafe_wait.title: Don't go out in unsafe conditions
fn_vent_unsafe_wait.explanation: Ice, dark, or the storm makes the trip outside unsafe right now.
actions: Call a licensed HVAC pro or your gas utility and say the vent may be blocked.
Keep CO alarms on, and leave if one sounds.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_vent_unsafe_wait.avoid: Don't go out on ice or in the storm to clear vents.

fn_meter_iced.title: Call the gas company about the meter
fn_meter_iced.explanation: The gas meter or propane regulator is buried or iced. Ice there can affect gas pressure.
actions: Stay clear of the buried or iced gas meter or propane regulator. Do not brush, chip, heat, or touch it.
Call your gas utility or propane supplier now and describe the snow or ice.
If you smell gas or hear unexplained hissing, get everyone outside and call the utility emergency line or 911 from away from the equipment.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_meter_iced.avoid: Don't chip, kick, or melt ice on the meter or regulator.

fn_vent_ice_pro.title: Ice is inside or frozen to the pipe
fn_vent_ice_pro.explanation: The snow came off, but ice stays inside or frozen onto a pipe end.
actions: Call a licensed HVAC pro and say a furnace vent pipe is iced.
Keep CO alarms on, and leave if one sounds.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_vent_ice_pro.avoid: Don't chip, melt, or pour water on the pipes.

fn_vent_damaged_stop.title: Stop using the furnace
fn_vent_damaged_stop.explanation: A vent pipe outside looks cracked, sagging, or pulled apart. Exhaust could get back inside.
actions: Set the thermostat to Off.
Call a licensed HVAC pro today.
Keep CO alarms on, and leave if one sounds.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_vent_damaged_stop.avoid: Don't push pipes back together or tape them.

fn_vent_cleared_basic.title: Vents clear · heat is back
fn_vent_cleared_basic.explanation: You reported clearing snow and heat returning. That observation does not rule out another fault.
actions: Keep the exterior terminations unobstructed.
If heat stops again, call for service; do not reset it.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_vent_cleared_basic.avoid: Don't pile shoveled snow near the pipes.

fn_condensate_freeze_pro.title: The drain line is freezing
fn_condensate_freeze_pro.explanation: Ice in the drain tube can back water up and shut a high-efficiency furnace off. It needs freeze protection.
actions: Call a licensed HVAC pro and say the condensate drain is frozen.
Ask whether the trap and line need heat tape or a new route.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_condensate_freeze_pro.avoid: Don't use a torch, heat gun, or boiling water on it.

fn_condensate_pump_pro.title: The condensate pump may be full
fn_condensate_pump_pro.explanation: A full or beeping pump can shut the furnace off to stop a leak.
actions: Stay away from water and electrical parts.
Call a licensed HVAC professional or plumber about the pump and leak.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_condensate_pump_pro.avoid: Don't open the pump or furnace to drain it.

fn_code_rollout_stop.title: Stop using the furnace and report the flame-related warning
fn_code_rollout_stop.explanation: The matching chart you selected includes a flame-related condition. The cause is unconfirmed and needs professional investigation.
actions: Set the thermostat to Off.
Call a licensed HVAC pro today and give them the code.
Keep CO alarms on, and leave if one sounds.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_code_rollout_stop.avoid: Don't reset anything or open the furnace.

fn_code_flame_no_call_stop.title: Stop · flame when there shouldn't be
fn_code_flame_no_call_stop.explanation: The code interpretation reported by the homeowner includes flame without a heat call. The cause is unconfirmed.
actions: Set the thermostat to Off and call a licensed HVAC pro now.
Smell gas? Leave and call from outside.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_code_flame_no_call_stop.avoid: Don't open the furnace or touch the gas line.

fn_code_to_pro.title: Call a pro and give them the code
fn_code_to_pro.explanation: Record the full displayed code and exact equipment model without opening covers.
actions: Tell the service company the code, model, and what happened.
Do not deliberately clear error history. If a hazard appears, leaving and getting help takes priority over preserving a code.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_code_to_pro.avoid: Don't reset the furnace or open its doors.

fn_code_unlisted.title: Record the code for your service company
fn_code_unlisted.explanation: Codes vary by exact model and control board. No meaning has been confirmed for this code.
actions: Photograph an already-visible display or record the light through an existing window.
Send the full code and already-known model to a licensed HVAC professional.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_code_unlisted.avoid: Don't remove the door to find the chart.

fn_breaker_tripped_pro.title: A tripped furnace breaker needs a pro
fn_breaker_tripped_pro.explanation: A tripped or unexpectedly off furnace breaker needs investigation. The cause is unconfirmed.
actions: Leave the breaker as it is.
Call a licensed HVAC pro and say the furnace breaker tripped.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_breaker_tripped_pro.avoid: Don't reset the breaker or open the furnace.

fn_switch_off_on_purpose.title: Leave the switch the way it is
fn_switch_off_on_purpose.explanation: Someone may have turned the furnace switch off on purpose, or you're not sure.
actions: Ask who turned it off, and why.
Call a licensed HVAC pro if it was off for a repair, leak, or smell.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_switch_off_on_purpose.avoid: Don't turn it back on until you know why it's off.

fn_switch_on_basic.title: Switch back on · heat is back
fn_switch_on_basic.explanation: The furnace switch was off by accident. With it on, the furnace started.
actions: Keep the switch identifiable and accessible; do not cover it.
If the furnace stops again, call for service. Do not cycle the switch again.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_switch_on_basic.avoid: Don't switch it off and on again to test.

fn_propane_out.title: Out of propane: the supplier checks first
fn_propane_out.explanation: An empty propane tank requires your supplier to check the system before restoring service.
actions: Call your propane supplier and say you ran out.
Let them check for leaks and restart your appliances.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_propane_out.avoid: Don't open the tank valve or relight anything.

fn_propane_low_supplier.title: Order propane now
fn_propane_low_supplier.explanation: The gauge reads low. Running out stops the furnace and means a leak check before the gas goes back on.
actions: Call your propane supplier for a delivery today.
If the furnace still won't heat, start a new check.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_propane_low_supplier.avoid: Don't touch the tank valves or regulator.

fn_oil_out.title: Out of oil: call for delivery and service
fn_oil_out.explanation: An empty tank can draw air or sludge into the burner. It may need a tech after delivery.
actions: Call your oil supplier for a delivery and ask about a service visit.
Keep the thermostat on Off until then.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_oil_out.avoid: Don't press the red reset button on the burner.

fn_oil_lockout_pro.title: Oil burner locked out: call a pro
fn_oil_lockout_pro.explanation: The burner control's light says it locked itself out.
actions: Call your oil service company and tell them the light color and pattern.
Keep the thermostat on Off until they come.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_oil_lockout_pro.avoid: Don't press the red reset button, even once.

fn_filter_fit_basic.title: Filter fixed · retest
fn_filter_fit_basic.explanation: You reported correcting the filter fit. Heating response has not yet been confirmed. Follow the exact manual’s filter size, quantity, and direction.
actions: You reported restoring the recorded thermostat settings with the required filters installed and access closed. Observe one heating cycle only while the home has enough heat and nobody is at risk.
If useful heat does not return or the furnace shuts off again, call for service. Do not reset it.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_filter_fit_basic.avoid: Don't stack filters or run without one.

fn_mh_return_cleared_basic.title: Air path cleared · retest
fn_mh_return_cleared_basic.explanation: You reported removing an obstruction from an existing air path. The home type and duct arrangement do not establish whether heat is restored.
actions: Keep the existing room grilles, return openings, and any closet-door louvers unobstructed. Keep equipment covers closed.
Follow the equipment manual’s storage and clearance rules.
If useful heat does not return or the equipment shuts off again, call a licensed HVAC professional. Do not reset it.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.

fn_mh_crossover_pro.title: The crossover duct needs a look
fn_mh_crossover_pro.explanation: If the duct between the halves is down, crushed, or loose, heat escapes under the home.
actions: Call a manufactured-home installer or HVAC pro about the crossover duct.
Ask them to seal it and strap it off the ground.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_mh_crossover_pro.avoid: Don't crawl under the home to fix it yourself.

fn_mh_animals_stop.title: Keep away from animals under the home
fn_mh_animals_stop.explanation: Animals under the home can damage ducts and wiring.
actions: Stay out from under the home.
Call pest control, then an HVAC pro for the ducts.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_mh_animals_stop.avoid: Don't reach in or crawl under to look.

fn_mh_listing_card.title: Questions for a mobile-home furnace job
fn_mh_listing_card.explanation: Furnaces in manufactured homes must be listed for manufactured homes.
actions: Ask your installer: is this furnace listed for manufactured homes?
Ask whether the AC or heat pump is certified to pair with it.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_mh_listing_card.avoid: Don't buy a standard house furnace for a manufactured home.

fn_elec_staging_normal.title: Cool, then warm, can be normal
fn_elec_staging_normal.explanation: Many electric furnaces turn their heaters on in steps after the fan starts, so air warms over a few minutes.
actions: You reported warm air and rooms maintaining temperature; continue normal observation.
If useful heat falls behind or the equipment shuts off again, call a licensed HVAC professional. Do not reset it.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
fn_elec_staging_normal.avoid: Don't open the furnace panel or touch the breaker.

fn_hydro_fan_delay_normal.title: A short fan delay can be normal
fn_hydro_fan_delay_normal.explanation: Some hot-water air handlers warm the coil before the fan starts, so a short wait is normal.
actions: You reported warm air and rooms maintaining temperature after the delay. Continue normal observation.

actions: Call a licensed heating professional urgently. Describe the ice or leak and the location of the air handler.

actions: Ask the installer to verify thermostat compatibility, configuration, and any active warranty.

sw_co_symptom_exit.title: Get everyone outside to fresh air now.
sw_co_symptom_exit.body:
1. Get everyone, including pets, out of the house now. Don't stop to open windows or look for the problem.
2. From outside, call 911 or your fire department. If anyone is very sleepy, confused, vomiting, has chest pain, or passes out, call 911 right away.
3. Don't go back inside until the fire department or your gas utility says it's OK.
4. Anyone with symptoms should get checked by a doctor, even if they feel better outside. Tell them you may have been exposed to carbon monoxide.
5. In an emergency, call 911 first. For questions about symptoms when it isn't an emergency, call Poison Control: U.S. 1-800-222-1222. Canada 1-844-POISON-X (1-844-764-7669). Quebec 1-800-463-5060. Nunavut: your local health centre.
6. Before using the heat again, have a licensed HVAC professional check the system.

fn_smell_dust_normal.title: A dusty smell can fade
fn_smell_dust_normal.body: A dusty smell the first few times the heat runs each season is common. Dust on the heating parts burns off. It should fade in about an hour of running. wh_gas_smell.title: Leave now and call from outside
wh_gas_smell.explanation: Gas, flammable vapors, or an unexplained strong smell near a water heater can mean immediate danger.
actions: Get everyone and pets outside.
Do not use a phone, switch, thermostat, or flame inside. Do not look for the source.
From outside, call the gas utility emergency line or 911.
Wait for emergency responders to say you may return.
wh_gas_smell.avoid: Do not operate gas controls, relight a pilot, or turn the appliance on.

wh_co_alarm.title: Get everyone outside to fresh air
wh_co_alarm.explanation: A CO alarm or possible CO symptoms need immediate attention.
actions: Leave now.
Call 911 or the fire department from outside.
Do not return until responders say you may.
wh_co_alarm.avoid: Do not silence the alarm and stay inside.

wh_burning_sparks.title: Leave and call 911
wh_burning_sparks.explanation: Smoke, burning, sparks, or flames outside the appliance can mean a fire.
actions: Get everyone and pets outside.
Call 911 from outside.
Wait for responders before returning.
wh_burning_sparks.avoid: Do not operate equipment or investigate the source.

wh_water_electrical.title: Stay away from water and electrical equipment
wh_water_electrical.explanation: Water near electrical parts or previously flooded equipment must not be used.
actions: Stay out of the water and away from the appliance.
For sparks, rising water, or immediate danger, leave and call 911 from outside.
Call a licensed water heater professional before any use resumes.
wh_water_electrical.avoid: Do not touch switches, cords, breakers, or the wet equipment.

wh_vent_damage.title: Stop using hot water and get help
wh_vent_damage.explanation: Soot, exhaust fumes, scorching, or a damaged vent can indicate combustion or venting problems.
actions: If there are fumes, a CO alarm, gas smell, smoke, or illness, get everyone out and call 911 from outside.
Keep away from the appliance and call a licensed water heater professional for urgent guidance.
wh_vent_damage.avoid: Do not touch vents, open covers, relight a pilot, or operate gas controls.

wh_scald.title: Care for the burned person first
wh_scald.explanation: Do not keep testing the hot water.
actions: Move away from the hot water.
For a serious burn, a large affected area, or uncertainty about severity, get urgent medical help or call 911.
Arrange professional inspection before using unusually hot water again.
wh_scald.avoid: Do not change a gas valve, mixing valve, or hidden thermostat.

wh_gate_unsure.title: Stop and get professional help
wh_gate_unsure.explanation: A hazard has not been ruled out.
actions: For possible gas, fumes, CO, fire, or illness, get outside and call for emergency help.
Otherwise stay away and contact a licensed plumber or water heater professional.
wh_gate_unsure.avoid: Do not approach equipment to prove an answer.

wh_relief_valve.title: Keep clear of the relief discharge
wh_relief_valve.explanation: A drip needs inspection; escaping hot water or steam can scald. The cause is unconfirmed.
actions: Keep people away and leave the outlet unobstructed.
Call a licensed plumber or water heater professional now. For uncontrolled steam, spraying hot water, or immediate danger, move away and call emergency services.
wh_relief_valve.avoid: Do not lift the lever, cap the pipe, close appliance valves, or drain the heater.

wh_tank_leak.title: Call a plumber about the leak
wh_tank_leak.explanation: The source and extent of the leak need inspection.
actions: Stay away from water and electrical equipment.
Call a licensed plumber or water heater professional promptly. Tell them whether water is spreading.
wh_tank_leak.avoid: Do not open covers, use the drain valve, or operate the heater’s water valves.

wh_frozen.title: Leave frozen equipment stopped
wh_frozen.explanation: Freeze damage can affect pipes and internal components even when no crack is visible.
actions: Call a licensed plumber or water heater professional urgently.
Keep people away from leaks and electrical equipment.
wh_frozen.avoid: Do not thaw with a torch, heat gun, or boiling water, and do not restart the appliance.

wh_rumble.title: Report the unusual noise
wh_rumble.explanation: A noise alone does not confirm sediment or another particular cause.
actions: Stop this check and call a licensed water heater professional.

wh_rumble.avoid: Do not drain, flush, or reset the heater to investigate.

wh_hydro_delivery_pro.title: Have the water-heater and coil connection checked
wh_hydro_delivery_pro.explanation: The guide has not confirmed water temperature or circulation through the air-handler coil. Tap hot water and room heat can behave differently.
actions: Call a licensed heating professional who services water-heater-fed air handlers. Report the heater type, tap-water behavior, airflow, and visible code.
Ask them to check this installation’s heat-source, circulation, and coil controls. Do not adjust them yourself.
If the home is losing needed heat, arrange urgent service and get anyone at risk somewhere warm first.

Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.

wh_too_hot.title: Stop using unexpectedly hot water
wh_too_hot.explanation: There is a scalding risk. A displayed setting does not prove the temperature at the tap.
actions: Keep people away from the hot water and call a licensed plumber or water heater professional.
If anyone is burned, care for them first and seek medical help.
wh_too_hot.avoid: Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, lift a relief-valve lever, drain or flush, or reset a breaker or safety control.

wh_one_fixture.title: Report the affected fixture
wh_one_fixture.explanation: A problem at one fixture can involve its mixing control or plumbing. This does not confirm the water heater works.
actions: Tell a plumber which fixtures are affected and whether the issue is recent.
wh_one_fixture.avoid: Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, lift a relief-valve lever, drain or flush, or reset a breaker or safety control.

wh_recovery.title: Record demand and recovery
wh_recovery.explanation: Storage volume and recovery rate vary by model and operating mode. A universal waiting time would be misleading.
actions: Use the recovery information in your exact owner’s manual.
If the problem occurs under ordinary demand, contact a professional. Do not raise temperature as a workaround.
wh_recovery.avoid: Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, lift a relief-valve lever, drain or flush, or reset a breaker or safety control.

wh_low_flow.title: Record the short-draw or low-flow pattern
wh_low_flow.explanation: Some tankless heaters require a minimum flow, but the threshold depends on the exact model. This symptom alone does not confirm a flow fault.
actions: Tell a professional which fixtures and draw lengths are affected.
Do not remove flow restrictors, change service valves, or raise temperature to test it.
wh_low_flow.avoid: Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, lift a relief-valve lever, drain or flush, or reset a breaker or safety control.

wh_recirc.title: Record the delay and recirculation settings
wh_recirc.explanation: Pipe distance, demand, and recirculation setup can affect the wait. The cause has not been confirmed.
actions: Photograph the normal user display and record when the delay happens.
Use the exact manual or installer for recirculation and mode changes; do not enter installer menus.
wh_recirc.avoid: Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, lift a relief-valve lever, drain or flush, or reset a breaker or safety control.

wh_code_pro.title: Give the professional the full code
wh_code_pro.explanation: A code needs the exact model and control context.
actions: Share the full code, model, timing, and any already-observed leak or noise.
Do not reset it just to see whether it returns.
wh_code_pro.avoid: Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, lift a relief-valve lever, drain or flush, or reset a breaker or safety control.

wh_power_pro.title: Leave power controls as they are
wh_power_pro.explanation: A dark display or possible trip needs professional investigation.
actions: Call a licensed water heater professional or electrician. Report whether a breaker or GFCI appeared tripped.
wh_power_pro.avoid: Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, lift a relief-valve lever, drain or flush, or reset a breaker or safety control.

wh_pilot_pro.title: Have the pilot problem checked
wh_pilot_pro.explanation: An extinguished pilot needs an equipment-specific inspection.
actions: Call the gas utility or a licensed water heater professional.

wh_pilot_pro.avoid: Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, lift a relief-valve lever, drain or flush, or reset a breaker or safety control.

wh_airpath.title: Keep the water heater’s air path clear
wh_airpath.explanation: Heat pump water heaters need the air volume and clearance specified for the installation.
actions: Move ordinary stored objects only if you can do so without going near a hazard. Follow the clearance in the exact manual.
Do not remove the top cover, duct the unit, or change installation openings.
wh_airpath.avoid: Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, lift a relief-valve lever, drain or flush, or reset a breaker or safety control.

wh_filter_observed.title: Record the cleared filter reminder
wh_filter_observed.explanation: You reported the reminder clearing after following your manual. This does not prove heating performance is restored.
actions: If hot water remains insufficient or the reminder returns, contact a professional.
wh_filter_observed.avoid: Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, lift a relief-valve lever, drain or flush, or reset a breaker or safety control.

wh_call_pro.title: Prepare for a water-heater service call
wh_call_pro.explanation: The cause has not been confirmed.
actions: Tell the professional the heater type, exact model if already known, affected fixtures, timing, and any visible code.
New smell, CO alarm, smoke, steam, or water near electrical parts takes priority; use Stop / get help.
wh_call_pro.avoid: Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, lift a relief-valve lever, drain or flush, or reset a breaker or safety control.

co: Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of anything that can burn.
